  associated_asset_asset_registry_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid asset (substation, transformer, generator, transmission line, distribution feeder, capacitor bank, etc.) that this SCADA point monitors or controls. Links the telemetry point to the physical asset in the asset management system (Maximo EAM or Esri ArcGIS). Used for asset health analytics and outage correlation.']
  associated_asset_registry_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid asset (substation, transformer, generator, transmission line, distribution feeder, capacitor bank, etc.) that this SCADA point monitors or controls. Links the telemetry point to the physical asset in the asset management system (Maximo EAM or Esri ArcGIS). Used for asset health analytics and outage correlation.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: SCADA points are located within a balancing area; linking provides spatial context and removes string field.']
  it_asset_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to technology.it_asset. Business justification: Each SCADA point corresponds to a physical IT asset (sensor/device); linking supports maintenance schedules and regulatory asset tracking.']
  network_device_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to technology.network_device. Business justification: SCADA points are collected via network devices; linking enables IT asset management and cybersecurity compliance for each point.']
  resource_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to der.der_resource. Business justification: SCADA points monitor DER inverter output for real‑time operations; utility operators need this link for dispatch and compliance.']
  transmission_substation_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the substation or switching station where the field device associated with this SCADA point is physically located. Used for geographic grouping, outage management correlation, and NERC reliability reporting. Links to the substation master record in GIS and EMS network model.']
  alarm_high_high_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The critical upper threshold (High-High) above which an emergency or critical alarm is triggered, indicating a severe operational condition requiring immediate operator action. Expressed in engineering units. Used in EMS/DMS for two-tier alarm escalation (High vs. High-High). Supports NERC reliability event classification.']
  alarm_high_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The upper operational threshold above which an alarm condition is triggered in the EMS/DMS/SCADA system. When the measured value exceeds this limit, an alarm notification is generated for grid operators. Expressed in engineering units. Configured in GE PowerOn EMS/DMS alarm management module.']
  alarm_low_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The lower operational threshold below which an alarm condition is triggered in the EMS/DMS/SCADA system. When the measured value falls below this limit, an alarm notification is generated for grid operators. Expressed in engineering units. Configured in GE PowerOn EMS/DMS alarm management module.']
  alarm_low_low_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The critical lower threshold (Low-Low) below which an emergency or critical alarm is triggered, indicating a severe operational condition requiring immediate operator action. Expressed in engineering units. Used in EMS/DMS for two-tier alarm escalation (Low vs. Low-Low). Supports NERC reliability event classification.']
  asset_class varchar [note: 'The operational asset class of the grid infrastructure element monitored by this SCADA point. Used for domain routing, regulatory reporting boundary classification, and T&D cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation|transmission|distribution|substation|gas_pipeline|gas_distribution|metering|protection — promote to reference product]']
  commissioned_date date [note: 'The date on which this SCADA point was formally commissioned and activated in the operational SCADA/EMS/DMS system. Marks the start of the point\'s active lifecycle. Used for asset age analysis, warranty tracking, and NERC CIP change management audit trails.']
  communication_protocol varchar [note: 'The communication protocol used to transmit telemetry data from the field device (RTU/IED) to the SCADA master station for this point. Common utility protocols include DNP3, IEC 60870-5-101/104, IEC 61850, Modbus, and ICCP for inter-control-center communications. Used for cybersecurity classification and NERC CIP asset categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DNP3|IEC60870-5-101|IEC60870-5-104|Modbus|IEC61850|ICCP|OPC-DA|OPC-UA — promote to reference product]']
  compression_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether OSIsoft PI Historian data compression (exception and compression deviation) is enabled for this point. When True, PI Historian applies the deadband_value and compression deviation to reduce storage while preserving data fidelity. When False, all scanned values are archived (raw storage mode). Impacts PI Historian storage sizing and data retrieval performance.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this SCADA point record was first created in the master catalog (Silver Layer). Represents the audit creation time in the Databricks Lakehouse. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise timestamp convention.']
  data_quality_code varchar [note: 'The current or last-known data quality status of this SCADA point as reported by OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS. \'good\' = valid telemetry; \'bad\' = communication failure or device fault; \'uncertain\' = questionable signal; \'substituted\' = manually overridden value; \'manual_entry\' = operator-entered value; \'out_of_range\' = value outside raw limits. Used for data quality filtering in analytics.']
  deadband_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The minimum change in the measured value required to trigger a new data archive event in OSIsoft PI Historian (exception deviation). Expressed in the same engineering units as the point. Prevents excessive data storage for slowly-changing signals while ensuring meaningful changes are captured. Configured per point in PI Historian compression settings.']
  decommissioned_date date [note: 'The date on which this SCADA point was decommissioned and removed from active scanning in the SCADA/EMS/DMS system. Null if the point is still active. Used for lifecycle management, historical data archival decisions, and NERC CIP asset retirement documentation.']
  ems_point_address varchar [note: 'The point address or database key used to reference this telemetry point within the GE PowerOn EMS/DMS real-time database. Typically a hierarchical address string (e.g., \'AREA.SUBSTATION.DEVICE.MEASUREMENT\'). Used for EMS state estimation, contingency analysis, and real-time display binding.']
  energy_type varchar [note: 'Identifies whether this SCADA point monitors an electric grid asset or a natural gas infrastructure asset. \'electric\' = electric T&D or generation; \'gas\' = natural gas pipeline, compressor, or distribution; \'both\' = dual-fuel or combined measurement point. Supports domain partitioning for electric vs. gas operations analytics.']
  engineering_unit varchar [note: 'The physical unit of measurement associated with the SCADA point value (e.g., \'kV\', \'MW\', \'MVAr\', \'A\', \'Hz\', \'degF\', \'PSI\', \'MCF/hr\', \'kWh\'). Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian engineering unit configuration. Critical for correct interpretation of telemetry values in EMS, DMS, and analytics applications. Aligns with IEC 61970 CIM unit symbols.']
  functional_location varchar [note: 'The SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) functional location code identifying the hierarchical physical location of the asset associated with this SCADA point (e.g., \'TX-SUBST-A-XFMR-01\'). Links SCADA telemetry to the SAP ERP asset hierarchy for O&M cost allocation, work order management, and CAPEX/OPEX tracking.']
  gis_feature_reference varchar [note: 'The unique feature identifier from Esri ArcGIS for the network element (substation, line segment, transformer, etc.) associated with this SCADA point. Enables spatial analysis, outage mapping, and geographic visualization of real-time telemetry in the GIS platform. Links SCADA data to the geospatial network model.']
  is_alarmed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether alarm processing is enabled for this SCADA point in the EMS/DMS alarm management system. True = alarm limits are active and will generate operator notifications; False = alarm processing suppressed (e.g., during maintenance or commissioning). Drives alarm display filtering in GE PowerOn EMS/DMS.']
  is_bes_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SCADA point is associated with a Bulk Electric System (BES) element as defined by NERC. BES-applicable points are subject to NERC CIP cybersecurity standards and NERC reliability standards reporting requirements. True = BES applicable; False = non-BES (distribution or sub-transmission).']
  is_cip_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SCADA point is subject to NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) cybersecurity standards. CIP-applicable points require access control, monitoring, and change management per NERC CIP-007-6. True = CIP applicable; False = not subject to CIP requirements.']
  is_controllable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SCADA point supports remote control operations (e.g., breaker open/close, tap changer raise/lower, setpoint adjustment) from the EMS/DMS/SCADA master station. True = remote control enabled; False = read-only telemetry. Critical for access control and NERC CIP classification of control points.']
  last_calibration_date date [note: 'The date of the most recent calibration or verification of the field instrument (transducer, CT, PT, transmitter) associated with this SCADA point. Used for instrument maintenance scheduling, data quality assurance, and OSHA/PHMSA compliance for gas measurement instruments.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this SCADA point record was most recently updated in the master catalog. Tracks configuration changes to point attributes (alarm limits, scan rate, deadband, etc.). Critical for NERC CIP-010-3 configuration change management audit trail and Silver Layer incremental load processing.']
  measurement_category varchar [note: 'The physical or electrical quantity being measured by this SCADA point. Categorizes the telemetry by measurement domain for analytics, display grouping, and regulatory reporting. Examples: \'voltage\' (kV), \'power_mw\' (real power), \'power_mvar\' (reactive power), \'frequency\' (Hz), \'flow_mcf\' (gas flow), \'pressure\' (PSI). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: voltage|current|power_mw|power_mvar|frequency|energy_mwh|flow_mcf|pressure|temperature|status_indication|position — promote to reference product]']
  next_calibration_date date [note: 'The scheduled date for the next calibration or verification of the field instrument associated with this SCADA point. Drives preventive maintenance work order generation in Maximo EAM. Ensures compliance with PHMSA gas measurement calibration intervals and OSHA instrument maintenance requirements.']
  nominal_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The expected or design nominal operating value for this SCADA point under normal grid conditions (e.g., nominal voltage = 138.0 kV, nominal frequency = 60.0 Hz). Used as a reference baseline for deviation analysis, alarm limit setting, and grid state estimation in EMS. Expressed in engineering units.']
  offset_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Additive offset applied after scale factor conversion to produce the final engineering unit value from the raw telemetry input. Used to correct for zero-point calibration errors or instrument biases. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS as part of the point\'s conversion formula.']
  pi_point_code varchar [note: 'The native point identifier (PI Point ID or PI Tag Name) assigned by OSIsoft PI Historian for this SCADA telemetry point. Used for direct API queries to PI Historian via PI Web API or PI OLEDB. Enables traceability from the Silver Layer back to the source historian record.']
  point_class varchar [note: 'Functional classification of the SCADA point indicating its operational role. \'measurement\' = real-time telemetry value; \'status\' = equipment state indication; \'control\' = remotely operable control point; \'setpoint\' = configurable operating parameter; \'alarm\' = alarm/event indicator. Used for access control, display filtering, and NERC CIP classification.']
  point_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the SCADA telemetry point providing additional context about what is being measured, the associated equipment, and its operational significance. Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian point descriptor field. Used in operator displays, engineering documentation, and data catalog search.']
  point_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the SCADA telemetry point as configured in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS. Serves as the primary identity label for the point (e.g., \'SUBST_A_BUS1_VOLT\', \'GEN_UNIT3_MW_OUTPUT\'). Used by grid operators and engineers to identify the measurement in real-time displays and historian queries.']
  point_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the SCADA point in the master catalog. \'active\' = currently scanning and reporting; \'inactive\' = configured but not scanning; \'commissioned\' = newly added and validated; \'decommissioned\' = retired from service; \'suspended\' = temporarily halted due to maintenance or fault. Drives data quality filtering in PI Historian and Silver Layer ingestion.']
  point_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the SCADA telemetry point by signal type. \'analog\' = continuous measurement (e.g., voltage, MW flow); \'digital\' = discrete state (e.g., breaker open/closed); \'accumulator\' = pulse-count integration (e.g., energy meter pulse); \'string\' = text-based status; \'calculated\' = derived value computed within the historian or EMS.']
  raw_high_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The maximum raw input value (in engineering units) that the SCADA point can physically receive from the field device before being flagged as out-of-range. Values above this threshold are treated as bad quality data. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS/DMS for data validation.']
  raw_low_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The minimum raw input value (in engineering units) that the SCADA point can physically receive from the field device before being flagged as out-of-range. Values below this threshold are treated as bad quality data. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS/DMS for data validation.']
  rtu_address varchar [note: 'The communication address of the Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) or Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) from which this SCADA point is polled. Includes protocol-specific addressing (e.g., DNP3 address, Modbus register, IEC 60870-5-101/104 information object address). Used for field device troubleshooting and communication diagnostics.']
  scale_factor decimal(18,6) [note: 'Multiplier applied to the raw telemetry input value to convert it to engineering units. For example, a current transformer (CT) ratio or potential transformer (PT) ratio applied to raw analog counts. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS as part of the point\'s conversion formula.']
  scan_rate_seconds varchar [note: 'The frequency in seconds at which the SCADA system polls or samples this telemetry point from the field device (RTU, IED, or PLC). Common values: 2 (high-frequency protection), 4 (standard SCADA), 30 (slow telemetry), 60 (non-critical). Determines data density in PI Historian and impacts AMI/SCADA bandwidth planning.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record from which this SCADA point configuration originates. Identifies whether the point is mastered in OSIsoft PI Historian, GE PowerOn EMS, GE PowerOn DMS, a field RTU/IED, DERMS, or OMS. Critical for data lineage, integration mapping, and Silver Layer ingestion pipeline routing.']
  tag_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique tag identifier assigned to the SCADA point in the source operational system (OSIsoft PI Historian tag name or GE PowerOn point address). This is the business identifier used across OMS, DMS, EMS, and PI Historian integrations to reference the telemetry point. Equivalent to the PI tag name in OSIsoft PI.']
  voltage_level_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'The nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the electrical bus, equipment, or circuit that this SCADA point is associated with (e.g., 500 kV, 230 kV, 138 kV, 69 kV, 12.47 kV, 0.48 kV). Used for voltage class filtering, T&D boundary classification, and NERC BES (Bulk Electric System) applicability determination.']

  Note: 'Master catalog of all SCADA telemetry points (analog and digital) monitored via OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS/DMS. Each record defines a measurement point including point name, tag ID, associated asset, engineering units, scan rate, deadband, and alarm thresholds. Serves as the SSOT for real-time grid telemetry configuration.'
}

Table gridops.scada_reading {
  scada_reading_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each SCADA telemetry reading or alarm event record in the Silver layer. Entity role: EVENT_LOG — this is an append-only stream of immutable timestamped observations and alarm events captured from SCADA points via OSIsoft PI Historian.']
  asset_registry_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the physical grid asset (transformer, breaker, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this SCADA point reading. Enables correlation of telemetry to the asset registry in Maximo EAM.']
  crew_member_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operator who acknowledged the alarm. Supports operator performance review, shift accountability, and NERC CIP-007 access logging. Null for non-alarm readings or unacknowledged alarms.']
  distribution_switching_order_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the switching order or clearance order in the DMS that initiated or is associated with a digital state change captured in this SCADA reading (e.g., breaker open/close operation). Links telemetry evidence to planned switching operations for post-switching verification.']
  dr_dispatch_dr_dispatch_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the Demand Response (DR) dispatch event that this SCADA reading is associated with, when the reading reflects load reduction or DR program response. Enables measurement and verification (M&V) of DR performance against dispatch instructions.']
  dr_dispatch_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the Demand Response (DR) dispatch event that this SCADA reading is associated with, when the reading reflects load reduction or DR program response. Enables measurement and verification (M&V) of DR performance against dispatch instructions.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operator who acknowledged the alarm. Supports operator performance review, shift accountability, and NERC CIP-007 access logging. Null for non-alarm readings or unacknowledged alarms.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the outage or reliability event record in the OMS (Outage Management System) that this SCADA reading is associated with. Links telemetry evidence to outage events for SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI calculation, post-event analysis, and NERC reliability reporting.']
  lmp_price_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the RTO/ISO pricing node (LMP node) associated with this SCADA measurement point. Enables correlation of real-time telemetry with Day-Ahead Market (DAM) and Real-Time Market (RTM) LMP prices for congestion analysis and energy trading settlement.']
  ot_asset_id varchar [note: 'The identifier of the Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) or Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) that collected and transmitted this SCADA reading to the EMS/DMS. Supports communication path diagnostics, RTU performance monitoring, and NERC CIP-007 device inventory tracking.']
  registry_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the physical grid asset (transformer, breaker, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this SCADA point reading. Enables correlation of telemetry to the asset registry in Maximo EAM.']
  resource_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to der.der_resource. Business justification: SCADA readings capture DER telemetry; required for performance reporting and regulatory compliance of distributed resources.']
  scada_point_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.scada_point. Business justification: Readings are generated by a specific SCADA point; FK enables direct join and eliminates need for point_name lookup.']
  transmission_substation_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the substation or grid node where the SCADA point is physically located. Supports geographic and topological analysis of grid conditions.']
  acknowledged_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The UTC timestamp at which the alarm was acknowledged by a grid operator. Used to calculate time-to-acknowledge (TTA) for operator performance review and ISA-18.2 alarm response time KPI measurement. Null if not yet acknowledged or not an alarm.']
  alarm_duration_seconds varchar [note: 'The elapsed time in seconds between alarm trigger (reading_timestamp) and alarm cleared (cleared_timestamp). Used for ISA-18.2 alarm flood analysis, chattering alarm detection (alarms clearing and re-triggering rapidly), and post-event reliability analysis. Null if alarm is still active or not an alarm record.']
  alarm_point_ref varchar [note: 'The unique identifier or tag reference of the SCADA alarm point as configured in the DMS/EMS alarm management system (e.g., \'ALM_SUB_NORTH_BKR101_THERMAL\'). Used to cross-reference alarm events back to the alarm rationalization register and ISA-18.2 master alarm database.']
  alarm_priority varchar [note: 'The ISA-18.2 priority level assigned to the alarm (critical, high, medium, low, advisory). Drives operator response urgency, alarm flood analysis, and alarm rationalization reviews. Null for non-alarm readings.']
  alarm_state varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the alarm per ISA-18.2 alarm management workflow (active = unacknowledged and in alarm, acknowledged = operator has acknowledged, cleared = condition returned to normal, shelved = temporarily removed from annunciation, suppressed = disabled by design). Null for non-alarm readings.']
  alarm_threshold double [note: 'The configured setpoint or limit value that, when crossed by the measured value, triggers the alarm (e.g., 110 MW thermal limit, 0.95 pu voltage low limit, 59.95 Hz under-frequency threshold). Supports alarm rationalization and threshold optimization analysis.']
  alarm_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the category of alarm event when is_alarm is True (e.g., thermal_overload, voltage_violation, equipment_failure, comm_loss, protection_operation, frequency_deviation). Null for non-alarm telemetry readings. Drives alarm rationalization and root-cause categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: thermal_overload|voltage_violation|equipment_failure|comm_loss|protection_operation|frequency_deviation|overcurrent|earth_fault — promote to reference product]']
  analog_value double [note: 'The numeric measured value for analog SCADA points (e.g., 345.7 kV, 150.3 MW, 60.02 Hz, 1250 amps). This is the principal EVENT_PAYLOAD_OR_VALUE for analog readings. Null for digital state points. Stored in the engineering unit defined by engineering_unit.']
  balancing_area_code varchar [note: 'The NERC-registered Balancing Authority Area code within which this SCADA point operates (e.g., the utility\'s registered BA identifier with NERC/FERC). Required for NERC reliability compliance reporting, RTO/ISO market settlement, and balancing area control performance (CPS1/CPS2) analysis.']
  cleared_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The UTC timestamp at which the alarm condition returned to normal and the alarm was cleared. Used to calculate alarm duration and time-to-clear (TTC) for post-event analysis and alarm flood studies. Null if alarm is still active or not an alarm record.']
  communication_protocol varchar [note: 'The SCADA communication protocol used to transmit this reading from the field device to the EMS/DMS (e.g., DNP3, IEC 61850, IEC 60870-5-104, Modbus, ICCP for inter-control-center). Supports protocol-level diagnostics and NERC CIP-007 communication security assessments.']
  compression_deviation double [note: 'The PI Historian compression deviation (swinging door algorithm tolerance) applied to this tag. Determines how aggressively PI compresses the time-series data. Understanding compression settings is essential for accurate signal reconstruction in load forecasting and post-event analysis.']
  digital_state varchar [note: 'The discrete state value for digital SCADA points representing equipment status (e.g., breaker open/closed, switch status, protection relay trip/normal, recloser enabled/disabled). Null for analog measurement points. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|closed|trip|lockout|normal|abnormal|on|off|enabled|disabled — promote to reference product]']
  engineering_unit varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for the analog_value (e.g., MW, MVAR, kV, Hz, A for amps, °C, psi, MCF). Ensures correct interpretation of numeric readings across different measurement types and supports dimensional analysis in grid operations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MW|MVAR|MVA|kV|Hz|A|°C|°F|psi|MCF|therm|%|pu|tap — 14 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  exception_deviation double [note: 'The configured exception deviation (deadband) value for this PI tag — the minimum change in analog value required to trigger a new archive event in PI Historian. A reading is stored only when the value changes by more than this amount. Used to understand data compression behavior and reconstruct continuous signal profiles.']
  ferc_jurisdiction varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the asset associated with this SCADA point falls under FERC jurisdictional transmission (interstate), state PUC jurisdictional distribution, or is exempt. Determines applicable regulatory reporting requirements for FERC Form 1, NERC reliability standards, and rate case filings.']
  ingested_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The UTC timestamp at which this record was written into the Silver layer lakehouse table. Used to measure data latency, detect backfill scenarios, and support audit trails. Distinct from reading_timestamp which reflects the real-world event time.']
  is_alarm boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this record represents an alarm event (True) or a routine telemetry reading (False). Partitions the dataset for alarm management workflows, ISA-18.2 alarm rationalization analysis, and operator performance review.']
  is_shelved boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the alarm has been temporarily shelved (removed from active annunciation for a defined period) per ISA-18.2 shelving practice. Shelved alarms are excluded from alarm flood counts but must be tracked for rationalization audits.']
  is_suppressed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the alarm is in a suppressed (by-design disabled) state, such as during planned maintenance or equipment outage. Suppressed alarms must be documented and reviewed per ISA-18.2 alarm rationalization requirements.']
  measurement_type varchar [note: 'The engineering quantity being measured by this SCADA point (e.g., MW for real power, MVAR for reactive power, kV for voltage, Hz for frequency, amps for current, temperature_c for equipment temperature, flow_mcf for gas flow). Drives unit-of-measure validation and alarm threshold interpretation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MW|MVAR|kV|Hz|amps|temperature_c|MVA|power_factor|tap_position|flow_mcf|pressure_psi|status — promote to reference product]']
  nerc_cip_asset_class varchar [note: 'The NERC CIP Bulk Electric System (BES) asset classification for the asset associated with this SCADA point (BES_high, BES_medium, BES_low, non_BES). Determines applicable NERC CIP cybersecurity standards (CIP-002 through CIP-014) and access control requirements for this telemetry data.']
  pi_archive_name varchar [note: 'The name of the OSIsoft PI Historian archive file or data archive from which this reading was extracted (e.g., \'PI_ARCHIVE_2024_Q1\'). Supports data lineage, archive retrieval for post-event analysis, and Silver layer backfill reconciliation.']
  pi_tag_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the PI Historian tag (SCADA point) that emitted this reading. Serves as the EVENT_SOURCE_REFERENCE linking the observation back to the originating sensor or control point definition.']
  point_name varchar [note: 'The human-readable PI tag name or SCADA point descriptor as configured in OSIsoft PI Historian (e.g., \'SUB_NORTH_BKR_101_STATUS\', \'GEN_UNIT3_MW_OUTPUT\'). Serves as the primary EVENT_TYPE_OR_CHANNEL discriminator and the operational label used by grid operators.']
  point_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the SCADA point as analog (continuous measurement), digital (discrete state), accumulator (pulse count/energy total), string (text state), or calculated (derived value). Determines how the reading_value and digital_state fields are interpreted.']
  quality_code varchar [note: 'OSIsoft PI Historian quality descriptor indicating the reliability of the reading (e.g., good = valid telemetry, bad = hardware/comm failure, uncertain = questionable signal, substituted = manually entered replacement, stale = no update within scan cycle). Critical for filtering unreliable data in operational analytics and NERC compliance evidence. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: good|bad|uncertain|substituted|manual|stale|comm_fail|out_of_scan — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  raw_value_string varchar [note: 'The original unparsed string representation of the SCADA point value as received from the RTU/IED before type conversion and engineering unit scaling. Preserved for data quality investigation, protocol debugging, and Silver layer reconciliation against the Bronze raw landing zone.']
  reading_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise UTC timestamp at which the SCADA point value was sampled or the alarm event was triggered, as recorded by OSIsoft PI Historian. This is the principal EVENT_TIMESTAMP and the primary time axis for all operational analysis, post-event review, and NERC compliance evidence.']
  rtu_code varchar [note: 'The identifier of the Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) or Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) that collected and transmitted this SCADA reading to the EMS/DMS. Supports communication path diagnostics, RTU performance monitoring, and NERC CIP-007 device inventory tracking.']
  scan_rate_seconds varchar [note: 'The configured polling interval in seconds at which this SCADA point is scanned by the RTU/IED and reported to PI Historian (e.g., 2 seconds for critical protection points, 30 seconds for non-critical analog measurements). Used to detect stale data and validate scan cycle compliance.']
  shelve_expiry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The UTC timestamp at which a shelved alarm is scheduled to automatically return to active annunciation. Supports ISA-18.2 shelving time-limit enforcement and alarm rationalization audit trails. Null if alarm is not shelved.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record that originated or forwarded this reading to the Silver layer (e.g., PI_Historian for OSIsoft PI, EMS for Energy Management System, DMS for GE PowerOn Distribution Management System, OMS for Outage Management System, DERMS for Distributed Energy Resource Management). Supports data lineage and cross-system reconciliation.']
  substitution_reason varchar [note: 'When quality_code is \'substituted\', this field records the reason the original telemetry value was replaced (e.g., manual_entry by operator, estimated from adjacent readings, comm_failure_fill during communication outage, maintenance_hold during planned work). Required for NERC compliance evidence and data quality audit trails.']
  time_to_acknowledge_seconds varchar [note: 'The elapsed time in seconds between the alarm trigger (reading_timestamp) and operator acknowledgment (acknowledged_timestamp). Pre-computed at ingestion time for ISA-18.2 alarm response time KPI reporting and operator performance review. Null for non-alarm records or unacknowledged alarms.']
  trigger_value double [note: 'The actual measured value at the moment the alarm condition was triggered (e.g., 112.5 MW when a 110 MW thermal limit was exceeded). Enables post-event analysis of how far the measured value deviated from the threshold. Null for non-alarm readings.']
  voltage_level_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'The nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the bus, line, or equipment associated with this SCADA point (e.g., 345 kV transmission, 138 kV sub-transmission, 12.47 kV distribution). Used to classify readings by voltage tier for T&D performance analysis and NERC FAC compliance.']

  Note: 'Near-real-time and historical telemetry readings and alarm events captured from SCADA points via OSIsoft PI Historian. Stores timestamped analog values (MW, MVAR, kV, Hz, amps, temperature), digital state changes (breaker open/close, switch status, protection relay operations), and alarm records. Alarm data includes alarm point reference, alarm type (thermal overload, voltage violation, equipment failure, communication loss, protection operation), priority level per ISA-18.2 alarm management standard, trigger value, threshold, acknowledgment status, acknowledging operator, shelving status, suppression state, and time to acknowledge/clear. This is the highest-volume product in the domain and the foundation for all real-time operational decisions, alarm management and rationalization, operator performance review, post-event analysis, NERC CIP-007 compliance, and NERC compliance evidence.'
}

Table gridops.ems_dispatch_instruction {
  ems_dispatch_instruction_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each EMS dispatch instruction record in the balancing area. Primary key for this entity.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the balancing authority area within which this dispatch instruction is issued. Aligns with NERC balancing area definitions.']
  bus_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the pricing node at which the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) applies for this dispatch instruction. Used for economic dispatch optimization and settlement calculations.']
  der_program_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to der.program. Business justification: EMS dispatch may include specific DER program instructions for ancillary services; operators need the program reference.']
  distribution_switching_order_id varchar [note: 'Reference to a switching order in the DMS (Distribution Management System) or EMS that is coordinated with this dispatch instruction. Used when dispatch is part of a planned switching sequence.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the EMS operator or system entity (AGC) that issued this dispatch instruction. Used for accountability and audit trail per NERC CIP and reliability standards.']
  generating_unit_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the generating unit or controllable resource to which this dispatch instruction is directed. Links to the asset registry in Maximo or GIS.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to an associated outage or reliability event in the OMS (Outage Management System) that triggered or is related to this dispatch instruction. Populated for reliability-driven dispatches.']
  operator_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the EMS operator or system entity (AGC) that issued this dispatch instruction. Used for accountability and audit trail per NERC CIP and reliability standards.']
  scada_point_id varchar [note: 'The SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) telemetry point identifier associated with the generating unit\'s MW output measurement in OSIsoft PI Historian. Used to correlate dispatch instructions with real-time telemetry data.']
  acknowledgment_status varchar [note: 'Status of the generating unit or resource operator\'s acknowledgment of this dispatch instruction. Pending indicates awaiting response; acknowledged confirms receipt; not_acknowledged indicates no response within the required window; rejected indicates the resource declined the instruction.']
  acknowledgment_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the generating unit operator or automated system acknowledged receipt of this dispatch instruction.']
  agc_sequence_number varchar [note: 'Sequential number assigned by the Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system for this dispatch instruction within a given AGC scan cycle. Used to correlate instructions to AGC telemetry cycles in OSIsoft PI Historian.']
  co2_emission_rate_lb_per_mwh decimal(10,4) [note: 'The estimated CO2 emission rate for the dispatched generating unit at the instructed MW setpoint, expressed in pounds per MWh. Used for environmental compliance reporting to EPA and state regulators.']
  compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the generating unit complied with this dispatch instruction within the required response time and MW tolerance. True if compliant; False if non-compliant. Used for NERC BAL reliability reporting.']
  contingency_name varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the N-1 or N-2 contingency scenario that triggered this dispatch instruction, if applicable. Used for post-contingency analysis and NERC reliability event reporting.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this dispatch instruction record was first captured in the Silver Layer data product. Audit trail field for data lineage and regulatory compliance.']
  demand_response_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this dispatch instruction targets a Demand Response (DR) resource rather than a traditional generating unit. True when the controllable resource is a DR program participant.']
  der_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this dispatch instruction targets a Distributed Energy Resource (DER) such as rooftop solar, battery storage, or small-scale generation managed via DERMS.']
  dispatch_reason varchar [note: 'The primary reason for issuing this dispatch instruction. Economic dispatch optimizes cost; reliability dispatch addresses grid stability; regulation dispatch supports frequency control; emergency dispatch responds to contingency events; voltage_support addresses reactive power needs; reserve dispatch activates operating reserves. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: economic|reliability|regulation|emergency|voltage_support|reserve — promote to reference product]']
  dispatch_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the dispatch instruction was generated automatically by the AGC system or issued manually by an EMS operator. Automatic instructions originate from AGC scan cycles; manual instructions are operator-initiated.']
  effective_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the dispatch instruction is expected to take effect at the generating unit. May differ from instruction_timestamp due to ramp lead time or scheduling offset.']
  energy_source_type varchar [note: 'The primary energy source type of the dispatched generating unit or resource. Used for generation mix reporting, renewable energy tracking, and REC (Renewable Energy Certificate) accounting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fossil_fuel|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|battery_storage|demand_response|other — promote to reference product]']
  expiry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this dispatch instruction expires or is superseded if not acknowledged or executed. After this time, the instruction is considered void.']
  frequency_regulation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this dispatch instruction is associated with frequency regulation service (AGC regulation signal). True when the instruction is part of a regulation up/down signal from the balancing authority.']
  fuel_type varchar [note: 'The specific fuel type consumed by the dispatched generating unit. Used for fuel cost allocation, emissions reporting, and EPA compliance. \'none\' for non-fuel resources such as wind, solar, or demand response. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas|coal|oil|uranium|water|wind|solar|none — promote to reference product]']
  heat_rate_btu_per_kwh decimal(10,2) [note: 'The heat rate of the generating unit at the dispatched MW setpoint, expressed in British Thermal Units per kilowatt-hour (BTU/kWh). Used for fuel consumption estimation, emissions calculations, and economic dispatch optimization.']
  instruction_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the dispatch instruction, used in operator logs, audit trails, and regulatory filings. Format: EMS-DISP-YYYY-NNNNNN.']
  instruction_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the dispatch instruction. Tracks the workflow from issuance through acknowledgment, execution, and completion or cancellation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: issued|acknowledged|executing|completed|cancelled|rejected — promote to reference product if additional statuses are needed]']
  instruction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the EMS issued this dispatch instruction to the generating unit or controllable resource. This is the principal business event timestamp.']
  lmp_at_dispatch decimal(10,4) [note: 'The Locational Marginal Price (LMP) in dollars per MWh at the dispatch node at the time this instruction was issued. Used for economic dispatch evaluation and post-dispatch settlement.']
  lmp_node_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the pricing node at which the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) applies for this dispatch instruction. Used for economic dispatch optimization and settlement calculations.']
  market_interval_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the energy market interval (Day-Ahead Market or Real-Time Market) associated with this dispatch instruction. Links to the market scheduling system or ETRM (Allegro) interval record.']
  market_type varchar [note: 'The energy market context under which this dispatch instruction is issued. DAM (Day-Ahead Market), RTM (Real-Time Market), bilateral contract, self-schedule, or none for purely reliability-driven dispatches.']
  mvar_setpoint decimal(10,3) [note: 'The target reactive power output level in Megavars (MVAR) instructed for voltage support purposes. Applicable when dispatch_reason is voltage_support or when reactive dispatch is co-optimized.']
  mw_actual_response decimal(10,3) [note: 'The actual MW output achieved by the generating unit in response to this dispatch instruction, as measured by SCADA telemetry from OSIsoft PI Historian. Used to assess dispatch compliance and unit performance.']
  mw_compliance_deviation decimal(10,3) [note: 'The difference in MW between the instructed setpoint and the actual response (mw_actual_response minus mw_setpoint). Positive values indicate over-generation; negative values indicate under-generation. Used for NERC compliance analysis.']
  mw_delta decimal(10,3) [note: 'The change in MW output instructed by this dispatch (mw_setpoint minus mw_setpoint_prior). Positive values indicate an increase in generation; negative values indicate a decrease. Used for ramp compliance analysis.']
  mw_setpoint decimal(10,3) [note: 'The target real power output level in Megawatts (MW) that the generating unit or controllable resource is instructed to achieve. This is the principal quantitative dispatch directive.']
  mw_setpoint_prior decimal(10,3) [note: 'The MW setpoint that was in effect immediately before this dispatch instruction was issued. Used to calculate the MW delta and assess ramp requirements.']
  operator_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes entered by the EMS operator at the time of dispatch. May include context for manual overrides, reliability concerns, or coordination with other control areas.']
  pi_tag_name varchar [note: 'The OSIsoft PI Historian tag name for the real-time MW output data stream of the dispatched generating unit. Enables direct linkage between dispatch instructions and PI Historian time-series data for operational analytics.']
  ramp_rate_mw_per_min decimal(8,3) [note: 'The instructed rate of change in MW output, expressed in Megawatts per minute (MW/min), at which the generating unit should ramp to the new setpoint. Derived from unit capability and AGC parameters.']
  regulation_direction varchar [note: 'Direction of frequency regulation service associated with this dispatch instruction. \'up\' indicates regulation up (increase output); \'down\' indicates regulation down (decrease output); \'none\' for non-regulation dispatches.']
  rejection_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason provided by the resource operator when a dispatch instruction is rejected or not acknowledged. Used for reliability event analysis and operator performance review.']
  reserve_type varchar [note: 'Type of operating reserve being activated by this dispatch instruction, if applicable. Spinning reserves are online and synchronized; non-spinning reserves can be brought online within 10 minutes; supplemental reserves provide longer-term backup.']
  response_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the generating unit reached or was confirmed to be at the instructed MW setpoint, as recorded by SCADA telemetry.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The originating operational system that generated this dispatch instruction. EMS for Energy Management System automated dispatch; AGC for Automatic Generation Control; DMS for Distribution Management System; OMS for Outage Management System; DERMS for Distributed Energy Resource Management System; manual for operator-entered instructions.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this dispatch instruction record was last modified in the Silver Layer data product. Used for incremental data processing and audit trail.']

  Note: 'Records each generation dispatch instruction issued by the Energy Management System (EMS) to generating units or controllable resources within the balancing area. Captures MW setpoint, ramp rate, dispatch reason (economic, reliability, regulation), issuing operator, and acknowledgment status. Integrates with AGC (Automatic Generation Control) and manual operator actions.'
}

Table gridops.load_forecast {
  load_forecast_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each load forecast record in the balancing area Energy Management System (EMS) forecasting engine. Primary key for the load_forecast data product.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the NERC-defined Balancing Authority Area (BAA) for which this load forecast was produced. The balancing area is the fundamental geographic and operational unit for which the EMS maintains load-generation balance. Links to the balancing area master reference product.']
  control_zone_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific control zone or load zone within the balancing area for which this forecast applies. Control zones represent sub-areas of the transmission system with distinct load characteristics, used for Locational Marginal Price (LMP) and zonal load forecasting.']
  weather_forecast_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.weather_forecast. Business justification: Load forecasts are derived from a specific weather forecast; FK links forecast source.']
  actual_demand_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The observed actual electrical load demand in Megawatts (MW) for the forecast interval, populated post-interval from SCADA telemetry or OSIsoft PI Historian. Null until the interval has elapsed and actuals are available. Used for forecast accuracy tracking and model performance evaluation.']
  confidence_interval_lower_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The lower bound of the statistical confidence interval for the forecasted demand in Megawatts (MW). Represents the minimum plausible demand at the specified confidence level. Used for probabilistic unit commitment and reserve margin planning.']
  confidence_interval_upper_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The upper bound of the statistical confidence interval for the forecasted demand in Megawatts (MW). Represents the maximum plausible demand at the specified confidence level. Used for contingency planning and operating reserve determination.']
  confidence_level_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The statistical confidence level expressed as a percentage (e.g., 90.00, 95.00) associated with the confidence interval bounds. Indicates the probability that actual demand will fall within the stated confidence interval bounds.']
  cooling_degree_days decimal(6,2) [note: 'The number of Cooling Degree Days (CDD) for the forecast date, calculated as the number of degrees the mean daily temperature exceeds 65°F. A standard weather normalization metric used in load forecasting models to quantify cooling-driven electrical demand.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording when this load forecast record was first persisted into the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and SLA compliance tracking. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  day_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the forecast day by its load profile category. Weekday, weekend, and holiday designations drive distinct load shape patterns in the EMS forecasting model. Peak day and off-peak day classifications support Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate analysis.']
  der_generation_forecast_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The forecasted generation output in Megawatts (MW) from Distributed Energy Resources (DER) including rooftop solar, behind-the-meter storage, and small-scale generation within the distribution system. Subtracted from gross load to derive net load. Sourced from DERMS forecasting.']
  dr_dispatched_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The amount of Demand Response (DR) capacity in Megawatts (MW) that has been dispatched or is planned to be dispatched during this forecast interval. Represents load reduction committed through DR programs, reducing the net load the grid must serve. Used for DR dispatch planning and DERMS coordination.']
  forecast_date date [note: 'The calendar date for which the load forecast applies. For day-ahead forecasts this is the operating day being forecasted. Used for daily operations planning, Day-Ahead Market (DAM) scheduling, and next-day unit commitment.']
  forecast_error_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The absolute difference between forecasted demand and actual demand in Megawatts (MW), calculated as actual_demand_mw minus forecasted_demand_mw. Positive values indicate under-forecasting; negative values indicate over-forecasting. Populated post-interval for accuracy tracking.']
  forecast_error_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'The forecast error expressed as a percentage of actual demand, calculated as (actual_demand_mw - forecasted_demand_mw) / actual_demand_mw * 100. Used as the primary KPI for EMS forecasting model accuracy assessment and NERC compliance reporting.']
  forecast_horizon_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the forecast by its planning horizon. Short-term covers hourly/daily intervals; medium-term covers weekly/monthly; persistence uses the last observed value as the forecast; day-ahead supports Day-Ahead Market (DAM) scheduling; real-time supports Real-Time Market (RTM) dispatch. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: short_term|medium_term|long_term|persistence|day_ahead|real_time — promote to reference product]']
  forecast_humidity_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The forecasted relative humidity percentage used as a secondary weather input to the load forecasting model. Humidity affects the heat index and cooling load, particularly for residential and commercial air conditioning demand.']
  forecast_interval_end timestamp [note: 'The ending date and time of the interval for which the load demand is being forecasted. Together with forecast_interval_start, defines the precise time window of the forecast. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  forecast_interval_start timestamp [note: 'The beginning date and time of the interval for which the load demand is being forecasted. For hourly forecasts this marks the top of the hour; for daily forecasts this marks midnight. Used for unit commitment scheduling, interchange scheduling, and DR dispatch planning. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  forecast_model_name varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the load forecasting algorithm or model used to produce this forecast (e.g., regression-based, neural network, ensemble). Supports model governance, audit trail, and comparison of forecast accuracy across different modeling approaches in the EMS.']
  forecast_model_version varchar [note: 'The version string of the EMS load forecasting model used to produce this forecast (e.g., \'3.2.1\'). Enables traceability of forecast outputs to specific model releases, supporting model validation, regulatory audit, and accuracy benchmarking.']
  forecast_model_version_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific version of the EMS load forecasting model used to produce this forecast. Enables accuracy tracking across model versions, supports model governance, and facilitates comparison of forecast performance between model iterations.']
  forecast_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for operational notes, qualitative adjustments, or override justifications applied to this forecast record by EMS operators. Captures manual interventions, special event adjustments (e.g., major sporting events, industrial shutdowns), or model override rationale for audit and review purposes.']
  forecast_run_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier assigned by the EMS forecasting engine to uniquely identify a specific forecast run or batch. Used to group all interval records produced in a single forecast execution cycle. Aligns with OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS run identifiers.']
  forecast_run_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the EMS forecasting engine initiated and completed the forecast run that produced this record. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the forecast was generated, distinct from the interval being forecasted. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  forecast_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the forecast record. Draft indicates the forecast is being generated; published indicates it has been released for operational use; superseded indicates a newer forecast run has replaced it; archived indicates it has been retained for historical accuracy tracking; cancelled indicates the run was aborted.']
  forecast_temperature_f decimal(6,2) [note: 'The forecasted ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit used as the primary weather input to the load forecasting model for this interval. Temperature is the dominant weather driver of electrical load in most utility service territories.']
  forecasted_demand_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The primary forecasted electrical load demand in Megawatts (MW) for the specified interval. This is the principal quantitative output of the EMS forecasting engine, used for unit commitment, interchange scheduling, and next-day operations planning.']
  heating_degree_days decimal(6,2) [note: 'The number of Heating Degree Days (HDD) for the forecast date, calculated as the number of degrees the mean daily temperature falls below 65°F. A standard weather normalization metric used in load forecasting models to quantify heating-driven electrical and gas demand.']
  interchange_schedule_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The scheduled net interchange in Megawatts (MW) with neighboring balancing areas or the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO)/Independent System Operator (ISO) for this forecast interval. Positive values indicate net imports; negative values indicate net exports. Used in balancing area control and unit commitment.']
  interval_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'The length of the forecast interval in minutes (e.g., 15, 30, 60, 1440 for daily). Determines the granularity of the forecast and aligns with Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) interval data and SCADA telemetry resolution.']
  is_peak_period boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast interval falls within a designated peak demand period as defined by the utility\'s tariff or operational planning criteria. Used to identify intervals requiring heightened operational attention, DR dispatch readiness, and capacity reserve verification.']
  is_reliability_event boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast interval is associated with a declared reliability event (e.g., emergency operating condition, NERC alert, extreme weather advisory). When true, the forecast may have been produced under emergency protocols with modified model parameters.']
  manual_override_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether an EMS operator manually overrode the model-generated forecast value for this interval. When true, the forecasted_demand_mw reflects an operator-adjusted value rather than the raw model output. Supports audit trail and model accuracy analysis.']
  net_load_forecast_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The forecasted net load in Megawatts (MW) after subtracting Distributed Energy Resources (DER) generation (e.g., rooftop solar, behind-the-meter storage) from gross forecasted demand. Net load is the actual generation requirement that dispatchable resources must meet. Critical for unit commitment and interchange scheduling.']
  operating_day date [note: 'The NERC-defined operating day (midnight to midnight local time) to which this forecast record belongs. Distinct from forecast_date in that it represents the grid operations scheduling day used by the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) for market and reliability purposes.']
  operating_reserve_requirement_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The minimum operating reserve requirement in Megawatts (MW) for this forecast interval, derived from the forecasted load and NERC reliability standards. Includes spinning and non-spinning reserves required to maintain grid reliability. Used for unit commitment and capacity planning.']
  peak_demand_estimate_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The estimated peak electrical demand in Megawatts (MW) expected within the forecast period. Critical for capacity planning, reserve margin calculations, and Demand Response (DR) dispatch planning. Used in General Rate Case (GRC) filings and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) submissions.']
  regulatory_reporting_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast record is designated for inclusion in regulatory reporting submissions (e.g., EIA Form 930, FERC filings, NERC reliability assessments, PUC rate case filings). Supports automated extraction of reportable forecast data for compliance workflows.']
  rto_iso_code varchar [note: 'The code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) market in which this balancing area participates (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP). Determines the market rules, scheduling protocols, and reporting requirements applicable to this forecast.']
  season varchar [note: 'The utility-defined operating season for the forecast interval. Seasonal classification drives load shape selection in the EMS forecasting model and aligns with seasonal rate structures, capacity planning periods, and NERC reliability assessments.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record that produced or supplied this load forecast record. Supports data lineage and provenance tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Values correspond to the utility\'s operational systems including the Energy Management System (EMS), SCADA, OSIsoft PI Historian, Distribution Management System (DMS), Outage Management System (OMS), and DERMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EMS|SCADA|PI_HISTORIAN|DMS|OMS|DERMS|MANUAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to this load forecast record, such as when actual demand values were populated post-interval or when the forecast status was updated. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  weather_adjusted_baseline_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The weather-normalized baseline load demand in Megawatts (MW), representing what demand would be under normal or reference weather conditions. Used to isolate weather-driven load variability from underlying demand trends for regulatory reporting and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) analysis.']
  weather_station_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the primary weather station or weather data source used to supply temperature, humidity, and other meteorological inputs to the load forecasting model for this forecast interval. Weather normalization is a core component of EMS load forecasting.']

  Note: 'Stores short-term (hourly/daily), medium-term (weekly/monthly), and persistence forecasts produced by the EMS forecasting engine for the balancing area and control zones. Includes forecasted MW demand by interval, weather-adjusted baseline, peak demand estimate, confidence interval, forecast model version, and actual vs. forecast variance for accuracy tracking. Used for unit commitment, interchange scheduling, DR dispatch planning, and next-day operations planning.'
}

Table gridops.frequency_regulation_event {
  frequency_regulation_event_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each frequency regulation event record in the balancing area. Primary key for this data product.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the NERC-registered Balancing Authority Area (BAA) in which this frequency regulation event occurred. Links to the balancing area master record for geographic and operational context.']
  crew_member_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operations control room operator who acknowledged, responded to, or closed this frequency regulation event. Provides accountability traceability for manual operator interventions and NERC compliance documentation.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operations control room operator who acknowledged, responded to, or closed this frequency regulation event. Provides accountability traceability for manual operator interventions and NERC compliance documentation.']
  regulatory_rate_case_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Frequency regulation performance is reported in rate‑case filings; linking each event to the rate case enables required reporting.']
  ace_threshold_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The ACE threshold in Megawatts (MW) that, when exceeded, triggers a compliance event or corrective action. Derived from the Balancing Authority\'s frequency bias setting and NERC BAL-001 control performance standards.']
  ace_value_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'Instantaneous Area Control Error (ACE) value in Megawatts (MW) at the time of the event. ACE represents the difference between actual and scheduled net interchange, adjusted for frequency bias. This is the authoritative ACE measurement for NERC BAL-001 real power balancing compliance.']
  actual_interchange_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The actual measured net interchange in Megawatts (MW) with neighboring balancing areas at the time of the event, as recorded by SCADA/EMS metering. The difference between actual and scheduled interchange is a primary component of the ACE calculation.']
  agc_response_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'Total Megawatts (MW) of generation adjustment dispatched by the Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system in response to this frequency regulation event. Represents the corrective generation signal sent to participating generating units.']
  baal_exceedance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) was exceeded during this event. True if ACE exceeded the BAAL threshold as defined in NERC BAL-001-2, triggering mandatory corrective action and potential compliance reporting.']
  baal_high_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The upper Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) threshold in Megawatts (MW) applicable during this event interval. Defined per NERC BAL-001-2 and used to assess whether the balancing authority exceeded its allowable ACE boundary.']
  baal_low_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The lower Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) threshold in Megawatts (MW) applicable during this event interval. Defined per NERC BAL-001-2 and used to assess whether the balancing authority exceeded its allowable ACE boundary on the under-generation side.']
  control_area_code varchar [note: 'NERC-assigned alphanumeric code identifying the Balancing Authority control area where the event occurred. Used in NERC compliance filings, RTO/ISO interchange scheduling, and energy balance reporting.']
  corrective_action_taken varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the corrective actions taken by the EMS/AGC system or grid operators to restore frequency and ACE to within compliance limits. Includes AGC dispatch instructions, manual operator interventions, and emergency procedures. Required for NERC BAL-002 disturbance control documentation.']
  cps1_score decimal(6,2) [note: 'NERC Control Performance Standard 1 (CPS1) compliance score as a percentage for the reporting interval. CPS1 measures the one-minute average ACE divided by the frequency error, with a minimum compliance threshold of 100%. Values below 100% indicate non-compliance with NERC BAL-001.']
  cps2_score decimal(6,2) [note: 'NERC Control Performance Standard 2 (CPS2) compliance score as a percentage for the reporting interval. CPS2 measures the 10-minute average ACE against the L10 limit, with a minimum compliance threshold of 90%. Values below 90% indicate non-compliance with NERC BAL-001.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time (UTC) when this frequency regulation event record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and ETL reconciliation.']
  disturbance_cause varchar [note: 'Root cause classification of the frequency regulation event or disturbance. Used for post-event analysis, NERC BAL-002 disturbance control standard reporting, and operational reliability improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation_trip|load_loss|transmission_fault|interchange_error|equipment_failure|weather_event|unknown — promote to reference product]']
  duration_seconds varchar [note: 'Total elapsed duration of the frequency regulation event in seconds, calculated from event_start_timestamp to event_end_timestamp. Used for NERC BAL-002 disturbance control standard compliance assessment and operational performance reporting.']
  ems_event_code varchar [note: 'The native event identifier assigned by the Energy Management System (EMS) — specifically GE PowerOn — for this frequency regulation event. Used for cross-referencing between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational EMS source system for audit and reconciliation purposes.']
  event_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to this frequency regulation event, used in NERC compliance filings, RTO/ISO settlement reports, and operational logs. Format: FRE-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}.']
  event_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (UTC) when the frequency regulation event concluded and normal operating conditions were restored. Null if the event is still active. Used to compute event duration for NERC BAL-002 disturbance control standard compliance.']
  event_severity varchar [note: 'Operational severity classification of the frequency regulation event based on the magnitude of frequency deviation, ACE exceedance, and system impact. Used for prioritizing operator response, escalation workflows, and post-event reliability analysis.']
  event_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (UTC) when the frequency regulation event began, as recorded by the Energy Management System (EMS) or SCADA historian. This is the principal real-world event time used for NERC compliance interval calculations and RTO/ISO settlement.']
  event_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the frequency regulation event record. \'active\' indicates the event is ongoing; \'resolved\' indicates corrective action has restored normal frequency; \'under_review\' indicates post-event analysis is in progress; \'reported\' indicates the event has been submitted to NERC/RTO; \'closed\' indicates all follow-up actions are complete.']
  event_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the frequency regulation event. Distinguishes between frequency deviations from 60 Hz, Area Control Error (ACE) exceedances, Automatic Generation Control (AGC) response actions, disturbance control events, regulation reserve deployments, and Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) exceedances. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: frequency_deviation|ace_exceedance|agc_response|disturbance_control|regulation_reserve_deployment|baal_exceedance — promote to reference product]']
  frequency_bias_setting_mw_per_hz decimal(10,3) [note: 'The balancing authority\'s frequency bias setting in Megawatts per Hertz (MW/Hz) in effect during this event. Used in the ACE calculation formula: ACE = (NIA - NIS) - 10B(FA - FS). Must be reported to NERC and the RTO/ISO per BAL-001 and BAL-005 requirements.']
  frequency_deviation_hz decimal(7,4) [note: 'Magnitude of frequency deviation from the 60 Hz nominal in Hertz (Hz). Positive values indicate over-frequency; negative values indicate under-frequency. Key metric for NERC BAL-003 frequency response obligation compliance and disturbance analysis.']
  frequency_nadir_hz decimal(7,4) [note: 'The lowest instantaneous system frequency in Hertz (Hz) recorded during this event, representing the frequency nadir following a generation loss or load increase disturbance. Critical metric for NERC BAL-003 frequency response adequacy assessment.']
  frequency_response_mw_per_hz decimal(10,3) [note: 'The balancing authority\'s measured frequency response in Megawatts per Hertz (MW/Hz) during this event. Compared against the NERC-assigned Frequency Response Obligation (FRO) to assess BAL-003 compliance. A more negative value indicates stronger frequency response.']
  interconnection_name varchar [note: 'Name of the North American electrical interconnection (synchronous grid) within which this frequency regulation event occurred. Determines the nominal frequency standard (60 Hz) and the pool of balancing authorities sharing frequency response obligations.']
  interval_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'End timestamp (UTC) of the energy accounting interval associated with this record. Paired with interval_start_timestamp to define the precise measurement window for energy balance and ACE compliance calculations.']
  interval_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Start timestamp (UTC) of the energy accounting interval associated with this record. Used to align hourly and sub-hourly energy balance data (generation, load, interchange, losses) with RTO/ISO settlement periods and NERC BAL-001 compliance measurement windows.']
  nerc_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this frequency regulation event meets the threshold for mandatory reporting to NERC under applicable reliability standards (BAL-001, BAL-002, BAL-003). True if the event must be included in NERC compliance filings or event analysis submissions.']
  nerc_violation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this event resulted in a confirmed violation of a NERC reliability standard (e.g., BAL-001 CPS1/CPS2 non-compliance, BAL-002 disturbance control failure, BAL-003 frequency response obligation shortfall). True triggers mandatory NERC self-report or enforcement action.']
  net_interchange_mwh decimal(14,4) [note: 'Net energy interchange with neighboring balancing areas during the event interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Positive values indicate net export; negative values indicate net import. Core component of the ACE calculation and energy balance accounting per NERC BAL-001.']
  pi_tag_reference varchar [note: 'The OSIsoft PI Historian tag name or tag path associated with the primary frequency or ACE measurement for this event. Enables direct traceability from the Silver layer record back to the real-time operational data stream in the PI Historian for validation and reprocessing.']
  regulation_down_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'Megawatts (MW) of regulation-down reserve deployed during this event to decrease generation output and correct an over-frequency or positive ACE condition. Reported separately for RTO/ISO market settlement and NERC BAL-002 compliance.']
  regulation_reserve_deployed_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'Total regulation reserve capacity deployed in Megawatts (MW) during this event. Includes both regulation-up and regulation-down resources activated to restore ACE to within compliance limits. Used for RTO/ISO settlement and reserve adequacy reporting.']
  regulation_up_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'Megawatts (MW) of regulation-up reserve deployed during this event to increase generation output and correct an under-frequency or negative ACE condition. Reported separately for RTO/ISO market settlement and NERC BAL-002 compliance.']
  reporting_interval_type varchar [note: 'The sub-hourly or hourly interval granularity for energy accounting data associated with this event record. Determines the resolution of generation, load, interchange, and ACE values stored. Aligns with RTO/ISO settlement interval requirements and NERC BAL-001 compliance measurement periods.']
  rto_iso_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) under whose market rules and settlement protocols this frequency regulation event is reported. Links to the RTO/ISO master record for market context.']
  scheduled_interchange_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The net scheduled interchange in Megawatts (MW) with neighboring balancing areas at the time of the event, as agreed through the interchange scheduling process. Used in the ACE calculation and compared against actual interchange to determine the interchange component of ACE.']
  settlement_interval_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the RTO/ISO market settlement interval record associated with this energy balance event. Links frequency regulation and energy accounting data to the corresponding Day-Ahead Market (DAM) or Real-Time Market (RTM) settlement period.']
  system_frequency_hz decimal(7,4) [note: 'Measured system frequency in Hertz (Hz) at the time of the event trigger. Nominal value is 60.000 Hz for North American interconnections. Deviations from 60 Hz trigger frequency regulation responses per NERC BAL-003 frequency response obligations.']
  system_losses_mwh decimal(14,4) [note: 'Estimated transmission and distribution system losses in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) during the event interval. Used in energy balance reconciliation: Generation = Load + Net Interchange + Losses. Supports NERC BAL-001 energy accounting and EIA reporting.']
  total_generation_mwh decimal(14,4) [note: 'Total electrical energy generated within the balancing area during the event interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Authoritative value for energy balance accounting, RTO/ISO settlement, and NERC BAL-001 real power balancing compliance.']
  total_load_mwh decimal(14,4) [note: 'Total electrical energy consumed by load within the balancing area during the event interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Used for energy balance verification, RTO/ISO settlement, and NERC BAL-001 compliance reporting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time (UTC) when this frequency regulation event record was most recently modified in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Tracks post-event corrections, operator annotations, and compliance status updates.']

  Note: 'Captures frequency regulation events, ACE (Area Control Error) exceedances, AGC response actions, and serves as the single source of truth for all energy balance and frequency compliance data for the balancing area. Records include: frequency deviations from 60 Hz, CPS1/CPS2/BAAL compliance metrics, regulation reserve deployment, and corrective actions taken. Also stores hourly and sub-hourly energy accounting: total generation (MWh), total load (MWh), net interchange (MWh), system losses, and ACE values by interval. Supports NERC BAL-001 (real power balancing), BAL-002 (disturbance control), BAL-003 (frequency response), energy balance reporting for RTO/ISO settlement, and operational energy accounting. This is the authoritative product for all ACE-related data, frequency compliance, and energy balance records.'
}

Table gridops.voltage_control_action {
  voltage_control_action_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the voltage control action record.']
  approver_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the supervisor or reliability coordinator who approved the voltage control action. Null if no approval was required.']
  approver_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the supervisor or reliability coordinator who approved the voltage control action. Null if no approval was required.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Voltage control actions occur within a balancing area; FK replaces textual code.']
  bus_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the electrical bus that was the target of the voltage control action.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operator who initiated the manual voltage control action. Null if action was automated.']
