  ems_dispatch_instruction_id varchar [note: 'The dispatch instruction identifier from the Energy Management System that authorized or triggered this voltage control action.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to an outage record if this voltage control action was related to outage management or restoration activities.']
  outage_gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to an outage record if this voltage control action was related to outage management or restoration activities.']
  primary_voltage_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operator who initiated the manual voltage control action. Null if action was automated.']
  registry_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific control device (capacitor bank, reactor, tap changer, or reactive power source) that was operated.']
  reliability_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to a reliability event record if this voltage control action was taken in response to a grid reliability event or contingency.']
  scada_point_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the SCADA monitoring point where the voltage control action was executed.']
  transmission_substation_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the substation where the voltage control action occurred.']
  verified_by_operator_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the operator who verified the successful completion and effectiveness of the voltage control action.']
  action_duration_seconds varchar [note: 'The time in seconds from action initiation to completion or failure.']
  action_mode varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the voltage control action was initiated manually by an operator, automatically by control system, scheduled as part of planned operations, or triggered by emergency conditions.']
  action_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes or comments entered by the operator or system regarding the voltage control action, including justification, observations, or special circumstances.']
  action_priority varchar [note: 'The operational priority level assigned to the voltage control action based on the severity of the voltage deviation and potential impact on grid reliability.']
  action_status varchar [note: 'The execution status of the voltage control action indicating whether it completed successfully, failed, partially completed, was aborted, or is pending verification.']
  action_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the voltage control action was executed in the grid.']
  action_type varchar [note: 'The type of voltage control action performed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: capacitor_bank_switch_on|capacitor_bank_switch_off|reactor_switch_on|reactor_switch_off|tap_changer_raise|tap_changer_lower|reactive_power_increase|reactive_power_decrease|voltage_regulator_adjust — promote to reference product]']
  ambient_temperature_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'The ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at the substation location at the time of the voltage control action.']
  approval_required_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator of whether the voltage control action required supervisory or reliability coordinator approval before execution.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when supervisory approval was granted for the voltage control action. Null if no approval was required.']
  automation_system_source varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the automated control system that initiated the voltage control action (e.g., DMS, DERMS, voltage regulator controller). Null if action was manual.']
  capacitor_bank_mvar decimal(10,3) [note: 'The reactive power rating in megavolt-amperes reactive of the capacitor bank that was switched. Null if action did not involve a capacitor bank.']
  control_algorithm varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the control algorithm or logic used to determine the voltage control action (e.g., volt-var optimization, conservation voltage reduction, local voltage control). Null if action was manual.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this voltage control action record was first created in the system.']
  generation_at_action_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The total real power generation in megawatts at the target bus or substation at the time the voltage control action was executed.']
  initiating_condition varchar [note: 'The operational condition or event that triggered the need for voltage control action.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this voltage control action record was last updated in the system.']
  load_at_action_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The total real power load in megawatts at the target bus or substation at the time the voltage control action was executed.']
  post_action_voltage_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'The voltage level in kilovolts measured at the target bus immediately after the control action was executed.']
  power_factor_post_action decimal(5,4) [note: 'The power factor measured at the target bus immediately after the voltage control action was executed. Value ranges from -1.0 to 1.0.']
  power_factor_pre_action decimal(5,4) [note: 'The power factor measured at the target bus immediately before the voltage control action was executed. Value ranges from -1.0 to 1.0.']
  pre_action_voltage_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'The voltage level in kilovolts measured at the target bus immediately before the control action was executed.']
  reactive_power_change_mvar decimal(12,3) [note: 'The change in reactive power in megavolt-amperes reactive resulting from the voltage control action. Positive values indicate reactive power injection, negative values indicate absorption.']
  reactor_mvar decimal(10,3) [note: 'The reactive power rating in megavolt-amperes reactive of the reactor that was switched. Null if action did not involve a reactor.']
  switching_order_number varchar [note: 'The formal switching order number associated with this voltage control action, if the action was part of a planned switching procedure.']
  tap_position_change varchar [note: 'The number of tap positions changed on a tap changer device. Positive values indicate raise operations, negative values indicate lower operations. Null if action did not involve a tap changer.']
  target_voltage_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'The desired voltage level in kilovolts that the control action was intended to achieve at the target bus.']
  verification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the effectiveness of the voltage control action was verified through post-action monitoring.']
  voltage_deviation_percent decimal(6,3) [note: 'The percentage deviation of pre-action voltage from the nominal voltage level, calculated as ((pre_action_voltage - nominal_voltage) / nominal_voltage) * 100.']
  voltage_profile_compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator of whether the post-action voltage level is within the acceptable voltage profile limits defined by regulatory standards and operational procedures.']
  weather_condition varchar [note: 'The prevailing weather condition at the time of the voltage control action, which may influence load patterns and voltage stability. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|cloudy|rain|snow|storm|extreme_heat|extreme_cold|fog|wind — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Records operator and automated voltage control actions taken within the grid including capacitor bank switching, reactor switching, tap changer adjustments, and reactive power dispatch. Captures target bus, pre-action voltage (kV), post-action voltage (kV), action type, initiating condition, and operator or automation source. Supports voltage profile compliance and post-event review.'
}

Table gridops.gridops_switching_order {
  gridops_switching_order_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the switching order record in the grid operations system.']
  approving_supervisor_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operations supervisor or reliability coordinator who reviewed and approved this switching order for execution.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: GridOps switching orders are tied to a balancing area; FK replaces textual code.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid operations control center operator who created and issued this switching order.']
  executing_crew_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the field crew or operations team assigned to physically execute the switching steps in this order.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the associated planned outage record in the Outage Management System (OMS) if this switching order is coordinated with customer outage notifications.']
  oms_outage_gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the associated planned outage record in the Outage Management System (OMS) if this switching order is coordinated with customer outage notifications.']

  purchase_order_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.purchase_order. Business justification: Regulatory cost allocation report requires linking each switching order to the purchase order that procured materials for the work.']
  transmission_substation_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the primary substation where the switching operations will be performed.']
  warehouse_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.warehouse. Business justification: Spare parts for switching orders are drawn from specific warehouses; linking enables inventory audit and cost tracking.']
  work_order_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the associated maintenance or construction work order that requires this switching order for equipment isolation or energization.']
  actual_completion_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The actual date and time when the final switching step in this order was completed and the order was closed.']
  actual_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The actual date and time when execution of the first switching step in this order was initiated by the field crew or control center operator.']
  affected_circuit_count varchar [note: 'The number of electrical circuits (feeders, transmission lines, or distribution circuits) that will be impacted by the execution of this switching order.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the approving supervisor or reliability coordinator formally approved this switching order for execution.']
  approving_supervisor_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the operations supervisor or reliability coordinator who approved this switching order.']
  cancellation_reason varchar [note: 'Detailed explanation of why this switching order was cancelled, including operational conditions, safety concerns, or work scope changes that led to cancellation.']
  cancellation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this switching order was cancelled or voided, if applicable.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this switching order record was first created in the grid operations system.']
  emergency_restoration_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether this switching order is part of an emergency restoration effort following an unplanned outage or system disturbance. True indicates emergency restoration.']
  estimated_customer_impact_count varchar [note: 'The estimated number of customer accounts that may experience service interruption or voltage fluctuation during the execution of this switching order.']
  issuing_operator_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the certified system operator who created and issued this switching order.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this switching order record was most recently updated or modified.']
  loto_tag_numbers varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) tag numbers applied to equipment as part of this switching order to ensure worker safety during de-energized work.']
  network_segment varchar [note: 'The segment of the electrical network where the switching order will be executed: transmission (high-voltage bulk power), distribution (medium/low-voltage customer delivery), substation (transformation and switching facilities), or generation (power plant interconnection).']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-form operational notes, special instructions, or additional context provided by the issuing operator or approving supervisor for this switching order.']
  order_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique switching order number assigned by the grid operations center for tracking and reference. Format: SO-YYYYMMDD-SITE.']
  order_purpose varchar [note: 'Detailed business justification and operational purpose for issuing this switching order, including work scope, equipment involved, and expected outcomes.']
  order_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the switching order: draft (being prepared), pending approval (awaiting supervisor review), approved (ready for execution), in progress (actively executing steps), completed (all steps executed), cancelled (order voided), or suspended (temporarily halted). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|approved|in_progress|completed|cancelled|suspended — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  order_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the switching order based on operational purpose: planned maintenance isolation, emergency fault restoration, fault isolation, load transfer, construction support, or equipment testing.']
  outage_coordination_required_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether this switching order requires coordination with the Outage Management System (OMS) for planned customer outage notifications. True indicates OMS coordination is required.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'Operational priority classification for the switching order: emergency (immediate safety or reliability threat), high (critical infrastructure), medium (scheduled maintenance), or low (routine work).']
  reliability_impact_assessment varchar [note: 'Documented assessment of the potential impact of this switching order on system reliability, including contingency analysis, N-1 criteria evaluation, and risk mitigation measures.']
  safety_clearance_required_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether this switching order requires formal safety clearance and Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) procedures before execution. True indicates safety clearance is mandatory.']
  scada_monitoring_enabled_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether real-time SCADA monitoring and telemetry is enabled for the equipment and circuits affected by this switching order. True indicates SCADA monitoring is active.']
  scheduled_completion_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The planned date and time when execution of this switching order is expected to be completed, including all steps and restoration.']
  scheduled_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The planned date and time when execution of this switching order is scheduled to begin.']
  sequence_validation_status varchar [note: 'Status of automated or manual validation of the switching step sequence for electrical safety, operational feasibility, and compliance with switching procedures: not validated, validated (passed all checks), validation failed (errors detected), or override approved (validation bypassed by authority).']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record that originated this switching order data (e.g., GE PowerOn DMS/OMS, SCADA EMS).']
  switching_procedure_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the standard operating procedure (SOP) or switching instruction document that governs the execution of this switching order, including document number and version.']
  switching_step_count varchar [note: 'The total number of discrete switching steps (individual device operations) defined in this switching order sequence.']
  voltage_class_kv decimal(10,2) [note: 'The nominal voltage class in kilovolts (kV) of the equipment and network segment affected by this switching order (e.g., 765, 500, 345, 230, 138, 69, 34.5, 13.8, 4.16 kV).']
  weather_conditions varchar [note: 'Documented weather conditions at the time of switching order execution, relevant for safety assessment and operational decision-making (e.g., clear, rain, snow, high wind, lightning).']

  Note: 'Manages switching orders issued by grid operations for planned and emergency switching sequences on the transmission and distribution network. Each order contains a header (order number, purpose, issuing operator, approving supervisor, execution status, safety clearances, LOTO tags) and an ordered sequence of switching steps (discrete actions on breakers, switches, and disconnects with per-step device identifier, action type, required safety tag, completion timestamp, executing operator, and sequence validation). Integrates with GE PowerOn DMS/OMS. Supports planned maintenance isolation, emergency fault restoration, and safety compliance tracking through granular step-level execution audit.'
}

Table gridops.switching_step {
  switching_step_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for each individual switching step record within the Databricks Silver Layer. Serves as the primary key for this entity.']
  authorizing_operator_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the control room operator or supervisor who authorized execution of this switching step. Supports two-person integrity requirements and chain-of-command compliance for high-voltage switching operations.']
  crew_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Each switching step is executed by a crew; linking enables tracking crew performance and safety compliance.']
  device_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific grid device (breaker, switch, disconnect, recloser, sectionalizer) on which this switching action is to be performed. Links to the asset registry in the Distribution Management System (DMS) or GIS.']
  distribution_substation_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the substation or switching station where the target device is physically located. Used for geographic and operational context in outage management and grid operations.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the operator or field technician who physically executed or confirmed execution of this switching step. Provides accountability and traceability for safety compliance and post-event analysis.']
  feeder_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the distribution feeder circuit associated with the device being switched. Enables load flow analysis and outage impact assessment at the feeder level.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the associated outage event in the Outage Management System (OMS) that this switching step is part of restoring or isolating. Links switching activity to customer impact and SAIDI/SAIFI metrics.']
  gridops_switching_order_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.gridops_switching_order. Business justification: Switching steps belong to an internal GridOps switching order; FK creates proper parent‑child link.']
  primary_switching_person_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the operator or field technician who physically executed or confirmed execution of this switching step. Provides accountability and traceability for safety compliance and post-event analysis.']
  scada_point_id varchar [note: 'The SCADA telemetry point identifier associated with the target device for this switching step. Used to retrieve real-time device status from the OSIsoft PI Historian or EMS/DMS SCADA system.']
  work_order_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the Maximo work order associated with the maintenance or construction activity that necessitated this switching step. Links switching operations to asset maintenance workflows.']
  action_type varchar [note: 'The discrete switching action to be performed in this step. Defines the specific operation on the identified device: open or close a breaker/switch, apply or remove a ground, or isolate/energize a section of the grid.']
  actual_execution_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The actual date and time at which this switching step was physically completed by the executing operator. Used for outage duration calculations, SAIDI/SAIFI reporting, and post-switching analysis.']
  arc_flash_boundary_ft decimal(8,2) [note: 'The calculated arc flash protection boundary in feet for the device associated with this switching step, as determined by arc flash hazard analysis. Defines the minimum safe approach distance for personnel.']
  communication_method varchar [note: 'The method used to communicate the switching instruction between the control room operator and the field operator for this step. Documents the communication channel for audit trail and NERC compliance purposes.']
  confirmed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the control room operator confirmed receipt of the completed step notification from the field operator. Captures the two-way communication verification required for safe switching operations.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this switching step record was first created in the system, typically when the switching order was drafted and steps were defined. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.']
  critical_customer_impacted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this switching step affects one or more critical customers (hospitals, emergency services, water treatment facilities, or other life-safety accounts). Triggers priority restoration protocols and regulatory notification requirements.']
  customers_affected_count varchar [note: 'The number of customer service points that are de-energized or affected as a direct result of this switching step. Used for outage impact assessment, SAIDI/SAIFI calculations, and customer notification prioritization.']
  deviation_reason varchar [note: 'Explanation for any deviation from the planned switching step, such as a step being skipped, reordered, or modified during execution. Required for post-event review and regulatory compliance documentation.']
  device_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name or label of the grid device targeted by this switching step, as maintained in the Distribution Management System (DMS) or GIS asset registry. Supports operator identification in the field.']
  device_state_after varchar [note: 'The verified state of the switching device immediately after this step was executed. Confirms the post-condition of the device and validates that the intended switching action was successfully completed.']
  device_state_before varchar [note: 'The verified state of the switching device immediately before this step was executed. Confirms the pre-condition of the device and supports post-event reconstruction of grid topology changes.']
  device_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the grid switching device targeted by this step. Indicates the physical type of apparatus to be operated, which determines the applicable operating procedure and safety requirements.']
  executing_operator_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the operator or field technician who executed this switching step. Captured at time of execution for audit trail and regulatory compliance purposes.']
  gis_feature_reference varchar [note: 'The unique feature identifier of the target device in the Esri ArcGIS geospatial asset management system. Enables spatial analysis, field crew navigation, and integration with the Distribution Management System (DMS) network model.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this switching step record was most recently modified, such as when step status was updated, notes were added, or execution was confirmed. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.']
  load_current_amps decimal(10,3) [note: 'The measured or estimated load current in amperes flowing through the device at the time of the switching step. Used to assess whether the switching operation is within the device\'s rated interrupting capacity.']
  network_model_node_code varchar [note: 'The node identifier of the target device within the DMS/EMS network connectivity model. Used for power flow analysis, load flow calculations, and topology processing to validate switching step safety.']
  ppe_required varchar [note: 'Description of the minimum Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) required for safe execution of this switching step, such as arc flash suit rating, rubber gloves class, and face shield requirements per OSHA and NFPA 70E standards.']
  protective_relay_coordination boolean [note: 'Indicates whether protective relay coordination checks are required before executing this switching step. Ensures that relay settings and protection schemes remain valid after the switching operation to prevent cascading failures.']
  remote_operation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this switching step was executed remotely from the control room via SCADA/DMS, as opposed to a manual field operation by a crew member. Distinguishes automated from manual switching for reliability analysis.']
  repeat_back_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the field operator performed a verbal repeat-back of the switching instruction to the control room operator prior to execution, as required by NERC operating procedures for safe switching.']
  safety_tag_number varchar [note: 'The unique identifier of the safety tag (hold tag, caution tag, or danger tag) associated with this switching step. Required for lockout/tagout (LOTO) compliance tracking and personnel protection verification.']
  safety_tag_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a safety tag (hold tag, caution tag, or danger tag) must be applied or verified before this switching step can be executed. Critical for personnel safety and OSHA compliance.']
  safety_tag_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the safety tag associated with this switching step. Distinguishes between hold tags (prohibit operation), caution tags (warn of hazard), danger tags (imminent hazard), and clearance tags (work authorization).']
  scada_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the device state change for this switching step was independently verified by the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, providing automated confirmation beyond operator verbal report.']
  scheduled_execution_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The planned date and time at which this switching step is scheduled to be executed, as defined in the approved switching order. Used for outage coordination and crew scheduling.']
  source_system_step_reference varchar [note: 'The native identifier of this switching step record in the originating operational system (GE PowerOn DMS/OMS). Preserves the source system key for data lineage, reconciliation, and cross-system traceability in the Silver Layer.']
  step_instruction varchar [note: 'Detailed written instruction describing the exact action to be performed in this switching step, including device location, access method, and any special precautions. Provides the field operator with unambiguous direction.']
  step_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for operator notes, observations, or deviations recorded at the time of step execution. Captures field conditions, anomalies, or explanations for skipped or failed steps.']
  step_number varchar [note: 'Sequential position of this switching step within the parent switching order. Defines the mandatory execution order of discrete switching actions to ensure safe and correct grid reconfiguration.']
  step_status varchar [note: 'Current execution lifecycle state of this individual switching step. Tracks whether the step is awaiting execution, actively being performed, successfully completed, skipped per approved deviation, failed, or cancelled.']
  step_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the nature of this switching step within the overall switching plan. Primary steps are the core switching actions; contingency steps are alternatives; restoration steps return the grid to normal; verification steps confirm device state; notification steps record required communications.']
  switching_purpose varchar [note: 'The operational reason or purpose for which this switching step is being performed. Classifies the switching activity to support reliability reporting, outage analysis, and regulatory compliance categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned_maintenance|emergency_restoration|load_transfer|fault_isolation|construction|testing — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]']
  voltage_level_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'The nominal operating voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the circuit or equipment associated with this switching step. Determines the applicable safety clearance distances, PPE requirements, and operating procedures.']

  Note: 'Individual step within a switching order defining a single discrete switching action (open/close breaker, isolate section, ground equipment). Captures step sequence number, device identifier, action type, required safety tag, completion timestamp, and executing operator. Enables granular tracking of switching sequence execution and safety compliance.'
}

Table gridops.gridops_outage_event {
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the grid outage event record. Primary key for the outage event entity in the Outage Management System (OMS).']
  asset_registry_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: Required for Outage Management Report: each outage event must identify the primary asset that caused the failure for regulatory reporting and restoration planning.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Outage events are scoped to a balancing area; FK provides relational integrity.']
  cost_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Supports Outage Cost Recovery and regulatory reporting by assigning outage events to a cost center.']
  crew_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Outage Management assigns a primary crew responsible for restoration; needed for outage restoration reporting.']
  filing_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.filing. Business justification: Regulatory outage reporting filing (e.g., FERC Form 1) requires linking each outage event to its filing for compliance.']
  incident_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.incident. Business justification: Regulatory outage report requires linking each outage event to a safety incident for compliance and root‑cause analysis.']
  incident_ticket_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to technology.incident_ticket. Business justification: Outage events generate IT incident tickets for system issues; linking enables root‑cause tracking and IT service level compliance.']
  purchase_order_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.purchase_order. Business justification: Repair work after an outage is often funded by a purchase order; linking supports restoration cost reporting and budgeting.']
  registry_id varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the specific equipment asset that failed. Links to Maximo EAM for asset history, maintenance records, and replacement tracking.']
  resource_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to der.der_resource. Business justification: Outage management tracks which DER resources are impacted to coordinate restoration and reliability reporting.']
  storm_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.storm_event. Business justification: Storm‑caused outages must be linked to the originating storm event for emergency response coordination and reporting.']
  vendor_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Outage restoration contracts external vendors; reporting (FERC/NERC) mandates identifying the vendor responsible for each outage event.']
  affected_feeder_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the distribution feeder (primary circuit) affected by the outage. Critical for outage location, crew dispatch, and reliability metric calculation by feeder.']
  affected_substation_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the substation serving the affected network segment. Used for outage aggregation, crew routing, and asset management coordination.']
  alarm_event_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the SCADA alarm that triggered or correlated with this outage event. Links to PI Historian and EMS for real-time operational data and root cause analysis. Also known as SCADA alarm ID.']
  confirmed_customers_affected varchar [note: 'Final confirmed count of customer accounts that experienced a service interruption during this outage event. Used for official SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI, and MAIFI calculations and regulatory reporting.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this outage event record was first created in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and change tracking.']
  crew_arrival_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when field crews arrived on-site at the outage location. Used to calculate travel time and time-to-repair metrics.']
  crew_dispatch_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when field crews were dispatched to investigate and restore the outage. Used to calculate response time metrics and crew utilization.']
  critical_infrastructure_affected_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether the outage affected critical infrastructure customers (hospitals, emergency services, water treatment, communications). Triggers priority restoration and regulatory notification.']
  customer_minutes_interrupted varchar [note: 'Total customer-minutes of interruption, calculated as the sum of (customers affected × duration) for each restoration milestone. Primary input for SAIDI calculation. Also known as CMI.']
  equipment_failed_type varchar [note: 'Type of equipment that failed and caused the outage (e.g., transformer, recloser, fuse, conductor, insulator, switch). Links to asset management for failure analysis and replacement planning.']
  estimated_customers_affected varchar [note: 'Initial estimate of the number of customer accounts affected by the outage, typically calculated by the OMS based on network topology and meter connectivity. Updated as outage scope is refined.']
  estimated_restoration_time timestamp [note: 'The estimated date and time when service is expected to be fully restored. Communicated to customers and updated as restoration progresses. Also known as ETR.']
  fault_isolation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the fault was successfully isolated from the rest of the network through switching operations. Enables partial restoration to unaffected customers.']
  first_restoration_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when service was first restored to any subset of affected customers, typically through switching operations or temporary measures.']
  major_event_day_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether this outage occurred during a Major Event Day as defined by IEEE 1366 2.5 beta method. MED outages are typically excluded from reliability metric calculations. Also known as MED flag.']
  oms_external_reference varchar [note: 'External identifier from the source OMS system (GE PowerOn). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracking. Also known as OMS external ID.']
  oms_source_system varchar [note: 'Name of the source OMS system that created this outage record (e.g., GE PowerOn, Oracle OMS). Used for data lineage and multi-system integration scenarios. Also known as OMS source system.']
  outage_cause_code varchar [note: 'Standardized IEEE 1366 cause code identifying the root cause of the outage (e.g., equipment failure, tree contact, animal contact, weather, vehicle accident, planned maintenance).']
  outage_cause_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the outage cause, including specific circumstances, equipment involved, and contributing factors. Captured by field crews during restoration.']
  outage_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Total duration of the outage event in minutes, calculated as the difference between outage start and end timestamps. Used for SAIDI and CAIDI reliability metric calculations.']
  outage_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when service was fully restored to all affected customers. Used to calculate total outage duration for reliability metrics and regulatory reporting.']
  outage_location_address varchar [note: 'Street address or nearest intersection to the outage location. Used for crew dispatch, customer communication, and regulatory reporting. Organizational contact data classified as confidential.']
  outage_location_latitude decimal(10,7) [note: 'Geographic latitude coordinate of the outage location in decimal degrees. Used for crew routing, GIS mapping, and spatial analysis of outage patterns.']
  outage_location_longitude decimal(11,7) [note: 'Geographic longitude coordinate of the outage location in decimal degrees. Used for crew routing, GIS mapping, and spatial analysis of outage patterns.']
  outage_number varchar [note: 'Business identifier for the outage event, typically generated by the OMS (GE PowerOn). Used for external communication, crew dispatch, and regulatory reporting.']
  outage_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the outage event was first detected or reported. This is the official start time used for SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI, and MAIFI reliability metric calculations.']
  outage_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the outage event. Tracks progression from initial detection through crew dispatch, fault isolation, restoration activities, and final closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: detected|confirmed|dispatched|isolated|restoring|restored|closed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  outage_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the outage event. Planned outages are scheduled maintenance; unplanned are unexpected interruptions; momentary are brief interruptions typically under 5 minutes.']
  peak_customers_out varchar [note: 'Maximum number of customers simultaneously without service at any point during the outage event. Used for storm impact assessment and resource planning.']
  regulatory_notification_required_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether this outage event requires notification to regulatory authorities (state PUC, FERC, DOE) based on customer count, duration, or critical infrastructure impact thresholds.']
  regulatory_notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when regulatory notification was submitted to the appropriate authority (state PUC, FERC, DOE). Required for compliance audit trail.']
  restoration_method varchar [note: 'Primary method used to restore service (e.g., switching, repair, replacement, temporary bypass, mobile substation). Used for restoration strategy analysis and resource planning.']
  storm_name varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the storm event if this outage was part of a named storm (e.g., Hurricane Ida, Winter Storm Uri). Used for storm impact analysis and FEMA reporting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this outage event record was last modified in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and change tracking.']
  weather_condition varchar [note: 'Weather conditions at the time of the outage event (e.g., clear, rain, snow, ice, wind, lightning, hurricane, tornado). Used for cause analysis and major event day (MED) classification.']

  Note: 'Master record for each grid outage event managed through the OMS (GE PowerOn), encompassing the full outage lifecycle from detection through restoration. Header captures outage type (planned/unplanned/momentary), affected network segment, cause code (IEEE 1366), estimated and confirmed customers affected, start timestamp, ETR (estimated time of restoration), and regulatory notification status. Includes a chronological restoration log tracking each milestone (crew dispatch, fault isolation, switching action, partial restoration, full restoration) with timestamps, restored customer counts, restoration method, and responsible crew. Serves as the SSOT for outage lifecycle management, SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI/MAIFI calculation, regulatory reporting (state PUC, DOE OE-417), and post-storm analysis.'
}

  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this restoration log record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this restoration log record was last modified. Tracks data currency and supports audit trail requirements.']
  restoration_cost_estimate decimal(15,2) [note: 'Estimated cost in USD associated with this restoration activity. Includes labor, materials, and equipment costs for financial tracking and storm cost analysis.']
  restoration_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Duration in minutes from outage start to this restoration milestone. Used for calculating CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index) and other reliability metrics.']
  restoration_method varchar [note: 'Method used to restore service at this milestone. Indicates whether restoration was via primary feed, alternate feed, temporary generation, or switching operations.']
  restoration_milestone_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the restoration activity milestone. Defines the type of restoration event being logged (crew dispatch, fault isolation, switching, partial or full restoration).']
  restoration_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes and observations recorded by field crews during restoration activity. Captures operational details, challenges encountered, and lessons learned.']
  restoration_sequence_number varchar [note: 'Sequential ordering of restoration activities within a single outage event. Enables chronological reconstruction of restoration workflow.']
  restoration_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this restoration activity. Tracks whether the restoration milestone is in progress, completed, failed, or pending verification.']
  restoration_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this specific restoration milestone occurred. Critical for calculating restoration duration metrics and CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index).']
  safety_incident_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a safety incident occurred during this restoration activity. True if any safety event was reported, false otherwise.']
  scada_confirmation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the restoration activity was confirmed via SCADA system. True if SCADA telemetry verified the restoration, false if manual confirmation only.']
  switching_order_number varchar [note: 'Reference number of the switching order executed during this restoration activity. Links to switching order management system for operational traceability.']
  vegetation_related_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether vegetation contact or interference was involved in the outage being restored. True if vegetation-related, false otherwise.']
  weather_condition varchar [note: 'Weather conditions present during this restoration activity. Supports correlation analysis between weather and restoration performance.']

  Note: 'Detailed chronological log of restoration activities for each outage event, capturing each restoration milestone (crew dispatch, fault isolation, switching action, partial restoration, full restoration). Records timestamp, restored customer count, restoration method, and responsible crew. Supports CAIDI calculation, regulatory reporting, and post-storm analysis.'
}

Table gridops.reliability_event {
  reliability_event_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the reliability event record. Primary key for the reliability event entity.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Reliability events are associated with a balancing area; FK replaces free‑text field.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Identifier linking this reliability event to associated customer outage records in the Outage Management System. Used for cross-system correlation and customer impact analysis.']
  incident_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.incident. Business justification: Major reliability events trigger safety incident investigations for regulatory reporting and corrective action.']
  oms_outage_gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Identifier linking this reliability event to associated customer outage records in the Outage Management System. Used for cross-system correlation and customer impact analysis.']
  affected_facilities varchar [note: 'List or description of transmission lines, substations, generation units, or other Bulk Electric System (BES) facilities impacted by the reliability event. Includes facility identifiers and equipment names.']
  analysis_completion_date date [note: 'Date when the post-event analysis or root cause investigation was completed. Null if analysis is not yet complete or not required.']
  caidi_impact_minutes decimal(10,2) [note: 'Contribution of this reliability event to the utility\'s CAIDI metric, measured in average minutes per customer interruption. Used for reliability performance tracking and regulatory reporting.']
  cip_incident_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this reliability event is also classified as a NERC CIP cyber security or physical security incident requiring separate CIP incident reporting. True if CIP incident reporting is required.']
  contributing_factors varchar [note: 'Additional factors that contributed to the severity or propagation of the reliability event. May include cascading failures, inadequate operating reserves, communication failures, or procedural gaps.']
  control_room_location varchar [note: 'Physical location or identifier of the control room where the reliability event was managed. Used for tracking operational responsibility and shift coordination.']
  corrective_actions_taken varchar [note: 'Description of immediate corrective actions taken by operators to mitigate or resolve the reliability event. Includes switching operations, load shedding, generation dispatch adjustments, and emergency procedures executed.']
  customers_affected varchar [note: 'Total number of customer accounts that experienced service interruption as a result of the reliability event. Used for outage impact assessment and regulatory reporting.']
  detection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the reliability event was first detected by control room operators, SCADA alarms, or automated monitoring systems. May differ from event start if detection was delayed.']
  ems_case_code varchar [note: 'Identifier for the EMS state estimator case or snapshot associated with the reliability event. Links to power flow analysis and system state data at the time of the event.']
  estimated_restoration_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Estimated date and time when full service restoration is expected to be completed. Updated as restoration work progresses. Null if event is already resolved.']
  event_classification varchar [note: 'Primary classification of the reliability event per NERC EOP/TOP standards and internal utility categorization. Determines regulatory reporting obligations and escalation procedures.']
  event_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time when the reliability event was fully resolved and normal operations restored. Null if event is still ongoing. Used to calculate event duration.']
  event_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique identifier for the reliability event, used in regulatory reporting and inter-utility communications. Typically follows utility-specific or NERC-prescribed numbering conventions.']
  event_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time when the reliability event was first detected or initiated. Represents the beginning of the disturbance or incident. Critical for NERC timeline reporting.']
  event_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the reliability event. Tracks progression from initial detection through investigation, containment, resolution, and final closure.']
  event_type varchar [note: 'Detailed type of reliability event such as transmission outage, generation loss, voltage deviation, frequency excursion, load shed, protective relay operation, or equipment failure. Provides granular categorization beyond classification.']
  frequency_deviation_hz decimal(6,3) [note: 'Maximum frequency deviation from nominal 60 Hz (or 50 Hz) observed during the reliability event. Measured in Hertz. Critical for assessing system stability and NERC BAL standard compliance.']
  initiating_cause varchar [note: 'Root cause or triggering event that initiated the reliability event. Examples include equipment failure, weather event, human error, cyber incident, protective relay misoperation, or external disturbance.']
  lessons_learned varchar [note: 'Summary of key lessons learned from the reliability event. Includes insights on operational procedures, equipment performance, communication effectiveness, and recommendations for improvement.']
  mw_generation_lost decimal(12,3) [note: 'Total amount of generation capacity lost during the reliability event, measured in megawatts. Includes forced outages and emergency shutdowns of generation units.']
  mw_load_lost decimal(12,3) [note: 'Total amount of customer load lost during the reliability event, measured in megawatts. Key metric for assessing event severity and NERC reporting thresholds.']
  nerc_oe417_report_number varchar [note: 'Unique identifier for the NERC OE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report filed for this reliability event. Links to official regulatory submission.']
  nerc_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this event meets NERC criteria for mandatory reporting under EOP-004 or other NERC standards. True if event must be reported to NERC.']
  notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the reliability event was formally notified to NERC, RTO/ISO, state PUC, or other regulatory authorities. Critical for compliance with reporting deadlines.']
  operator_entry_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the operator log entry by type. Distinguishes between event-related actions, routine observations, shift logs, standing orders, and equipment status notes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: event_action|observation|communication|shift_handoff|alarm_ack|switching_order|standing_order|equipment_status — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  operator_log_entry varchar [note: 'Chronological free-text narrative of operator actions, observations, and communications during the reliability event. Includes shift handoff notes, alarm acknowledgments, switching orders executed, and inter-utility communications. Forms the official auditable operational record.']
  operator_name varchar [note: 'Name of the control room operator who logged the entry or took action during the reliability event. Used for operational accountability and training purposes.']
  post_event_analysis_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a formal post-event analysis or root cause investigation is required for this reliability event. True for significant events requiring detailed technical review.']
  preventive_actions_recommended varchar [note: 'Recommended preventive actions to avoid recurrence of similar reliability events. May include equipment upgrades, procedure changes, training enhancements, or system reinforcements.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this reliability event record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this reliability event record was last modified. Updated whenever any field in the record changes. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']
  restoration_priority varchar [note: 'Priority level assigned for service restoration efforts. Critical priority for hospitals, emergency services, and critical infrastructure; high for large customer groups; medium and low for routine restoration.']
  rto_iso_region varchar [note: 'RTO or ISO region where the reliability event occurred. Examples include PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE. Used for regional coordination and reporting.']
  saidi_impact_minutes decimal(10,2) [note: 'Contribution of this reliability event to the utility\'s SAIDI metric, measured in customer-minutes of interruption. Used for reliability performance tracking and regulatory reporting.']
  saifi_impact_count decimal(10,4) [note: 'Contribution of this reliability event to the utility\'s SAIFI metric, measured as interruption frequency per customer. Used for reliability performance tracking and regulatory reporting.']
  scada_alarm_count varchar [note: 'Total number of SCADA alarms triggered during the reliability event. Used to assess event complexity and operator workload during the incident.']
  shift_supervisor_name varchar [note: 'Name of the shift supervisor on duty during the reliability event. Used for operational accountability and post-event review coordination.']
  state_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this event must be reported to state Public Utility Commission per state-specific disturbance reporting requirements. True if state reporting is required.']
  voltage_deviation_kv decimal(8,2) [note: 'Maximum voltage deviation from normal operating range observed during the reliability event. Measured in kilovolts. Used to assess voltage stability and equipment stress.']
  weather_conditions varchar [note: 'Description of weather conditions at the time of the reliability event. Includes temperature, wind speed, precipitation, lightning activity, and other relevant meteorological data.']
  weather_related_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the reliability event was caused or significantly influenced by weather conditions such as storms, lightning, ice, wind, or extreme temperatures. True if weather was a factor.']

  Note: 'Records NERC-reportable and internally tracked reliability events including disturbances, contingencies, N-1 violations, BES incidents, and all associated operator log entries and control room communications. Each event captures classification per NERC EOP/TOP standards, affected facilities, initiating cause, system impact (MW lost, customers affected), regulatory reporting obligation, and timeline. Includes chronological operator actions, observations, shift handoff notes, alarm acknowledgments, inter-utility communications, and free-text narratives forming the complete operational record. Also serves as the repository for routine operator log entries (shift logs, standing orders, equipment status notes) classified by entry type. Feeds NERC OE-417, state PUC disturbance reporting, NERC CIP compliance evidence, and serves as the official auditable operational record for all control room activities.'
}

Table gridops.dr_dispatch_event {
  dr_dispatch_event_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the demand response dispatch event. Primary key.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: DR dispatch events are executed within a balancing area; FK adds referential integrity.']
  compliance_obligation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Demand‑Response dispatches must satisfy a documented compliance obligation; the FK ties each dispatch to its obligation record.']
  customer_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: DR Dispatch Report requires linking each dispatch to the customer account enrolled in the program for settlement and regulatory compliance.']
  der_program_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the DR program under which this dispatch event was issued.']
  dr_enrollment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to customer.dr_enrollment. Business justification: Compliance audit tracks which specific DR enrollment was dispatched; the DR dispatch event must reference the enrollment record.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'The identifier of the grid operations control room operator who issued the DR dispatch event.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the outage management system (OMS) event that triggered this DR dispatch, if the dispatch was issued in response to a grid outage or contingency.']
  person_id varchar [note: 'The identifier of the grid operations control room operator who issued the DR dispatch event.']
  product_program_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.product_program. Business justification: DR dispatch events are executed under a specific demand‑response program defined in product_program; required for program performance tracking.']
  wbs_element_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Demand‑Response dispatches are tracked as projects; linking to WBS enables budgeting and cost tracking.']
  actual_mw_reduction decimal(12,3) [note: 'The actual measured load reduction in megawatts (MW) achieved across all participating resources, aggregated from interval meter data.']
  ambient_temperature_f decimal(5,2) [note: 'The ambient outdoor temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of dispatch, used for weather normalization and performance analysis.']
  baseline_methodology varchar [note: 'The baseline calculation methodology used to determine pre-event load and measure actual reduction: high 10 of 10 (highest 10 of last 10 similar days), mid 8 of 10, high 5 of 10, customer baseline (negotiated), or meter before/after (direct measurement).']
  compliance_status varchar [note: 'Overall program compliance status for this dispatch event: compliant (met all requirements), non-compliant (failed to meet targets), partial (some resources complied), under review (pending settlement), exempt (test or waived event).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this DR dispatch event record was first created in the system.']
  derms_integration_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this dispatch event was coordinated through the DERMS platform for DER-based DR resources.']
  dispatch_authorization_code varchar [note: 'The authorization code or approval reference for the dispatch event, required for emergency and economic dispatches per operating procedures.']
  dispatch_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'The total duration of the DR dispatch event in minutes, calculated from start to end timestamp.']
  dispatch_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The scheduled end date and time for the DR curtailment event.']
  dispatch_issued_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the DR dispatch event was issued by grid operations to participating resources.']
  dispatch_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text operational notes and comments recorded by the dispatch operator regarding event circumstances, special conditions, or post-event observations.']
  dispatch_number varchar [note: 'Business identifier for the DR dispatch event, formatted as DR-YYYYMMDD-NNNN for external reference and operational tracking.']
  dispatch_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The scheduled start date and time for the DR curtailment event.']
  dispatch_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the DR dispatch event: pending (notification sent, not yet active), active (curtailment in progress), completed (event concluded), cancelled (event aborted), failed (dispatch unsuccessful).']
  dispatch_trigger_type varchar [note: 'The operational reason for issuing the DR dispatch: emergency (grid emergency), economic (price-driven), capacity (resource adequacy), test (program validation), scheduled (planned event), or reliability (NERC compliance).']
  ferc_2222_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this dispatch event involves aggregated DER participation and is reportable under FERC Order 2222 requirements.']
  frequency_deviation_hz decimal(6,4) [note: 'The grid frequency deviation in hertz (Hz) from nominal 60 Hz at the time of dispatch, if the dispatch was triggered by frequency regulation needs.']
  grid_emergency_level varchar [note: 'The grid emergency alert level at the time of dispatch issuance, ranging from normal to emergency levels 1-3 per NERC EEA protocols.']
  iso_rto_market varchar [note: 'The ISO or RTO market jurisdiction under which this DR dispatch was executed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PJM|CAISO|ERCOT|MISO|NYISO|ISO-NE|SPP|non-ISO — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this DR dispatch event record was last updated, reflecting status changes, performance data updates, or settlement finalization.']
  lmp_trigger_price decimal(10,2) [note: 'The locational marginal price (LMP) in dollars per MWh that triggered an economic DR dispatch, if applicable.']
  notification_lead_time_minutes varchar [note: 'The advance notice time in minutes between dispatch issuance and dispatch start, as required by program rules.']
  notification_method varchar [note: 'The primary method used to notify DR participants of the dispatch event: automated signal (OpenADR, API), phone, email, SMS, web portal, or SCADA command.']
  performance_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The overall performance of the dispatch event expressed as a percentage of actual MW reduction divided by target MW reduction.']
  scada_snapshot_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp of the SCADA system snapshot captured at dispatch issuance, used for grid state verification and post-event analysis.']
  settlement_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'The total financial settlement amount in USD to be paid to all participating DR resources for this dispatch event, based on performance and program rates.']
  settlement_ready_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether all performance data has been validated and the event is ready for financial settlement and capacity payment processing.']
  target_mw_reduction decimal(12,3) [note: 'The total target load reduction in megawatts (MW) requested from all participating DR resources for this dispatch event.']
  total_resources_dispatched varchar [note: 'The total count of individual DR resources (customers, aggregators, DERs) that were dispatched as part of this event.']
  total_resources_responded varchar [note: 'The count of dispatched resources that successfully responded and achieved measurable load reduction during the event.']
  voltage_deviation_kv decimal(8,3) [note: 'The voltage deviation in kilovolts (kV) from nominal levels at critical substations, if the dispatch was triggered by voltage control needs.']
  weather_adjusted_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the baseline and performance calculations were adjusted for weather conditions (temperature, humidity) per program rules.']

  Note: 'Records each demand response (DR) dispatch event issued by grid operations to enrolled DR resources and aggregators, with full per-resource performance tracking. Header captures dispatch trigger (emergency, economic, capacity, test), target MW reduction, dispatch window, notification method, and overall program compliance status. Detail records capture each participating resource\'s identifier, resource type, nominated MW reduction, actual metered MW reduction (from interval meter data), response time, ramp compliance, performance score, and settlement-ready compliance flag. Integrates with DERMS for DER-based DR and with the product domain for DR program definitions. Supports DR capacity payment settlement, program compliance verification, FERC Order 2222 reporting, and resource performance trending.'
}

Table gridops.dr_resource_response {
  dr_resource_response_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the demand response resource response record. Primary key.']
  aggregator_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the aggregator entity if this resource is part of an aggregated DR portfolio.']
  dr_dispatch_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent DR dispatch event that triggered this resource response.']
  dr_resource_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific DR resource or aggregator that responded to the dispatch event.']
  product_program_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific DR program under which this response was dispatched.']
  actual_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'The actual duration in minutes that the resource sustained the load reduction.']
  actual_load_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The actual metered load in megawatts during the DR event period, measured from AMI or SCADA systems.']
  actual_reduction_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The actual measured load reduction in megawatts achieved by the resource, calculated as baseline minus actual load.']
  balancing_authority_area varchar [note: 'The balancing authority area code where this DR resource is located and responded.']
  baseline_calculation_method varchar [note: 'The methodology used to calculate the baseline load for this resource (e.g., 10-of-10, 5-of-10, regression-based).']
  baseline_load_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The calculated baseline load in megawatts representing what the resource would have consumed without the DR event, used for settlement calculations.']
  compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator of whether the resource met the minimum performance requirements for the DR event (True = compliant, False = non-compliant).']
  compliance_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of nominated reduction actually delivered, calculated as (actual reduction / nominated reduction) * 100.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this resource response record was first created in the system.']
  dispatch_instruction_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the dispatch instruction that triggered this response.']
  dispatch_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the DR dispatch signal was issued to the resource.']
  event_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'The total duration in minutes that the resource was expected to maintain the load reduction.']
  meter_data_source varchar [note: 'The source system or method used to capture the actual load measurements for this response.']
  nominated_reduction_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The committed or nominated load reduction in megawatts that the resource agreed to provide for this dispatch event.']
  non_compliance_reason varchar [note: 'Explanation or code indicating why the resource failed to meet compliance requirements, if applicable.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for operational notes, exceptions, or additional context regarding this resource response.']
  penalty_amount_usd decimal(15,2) [note: 'Financial penalty assessed against the resource for non-compliance or under-performance, if applicable.']
  performance_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Calculated performance score for the resource response, incorporating reduction accuracy, response time, and sustained performance. Used for resource ranking and future dispatch prioritization.']
  rebound_effect_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The measured load increase in megawatts immediately following the DR event, representing the rebound or snapback effect.']
  reduction_variance_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The difference between nominated and actual reduction in megawatts, used for compliance and performance assessment.']
  resource_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name or identifier of the DR resource or aggregator for operational reference.']
  resource_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the DR resource type participating in the event.']
  response_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The actual date and time when the resource completed its response to the dispatch event.']
  response_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The actual date and time when the resource began responding to the dispatch signal.']
  response_time_minutes decimal(8,2) [note: 'The elapsed time in minutes from dispatch signal to the start of measurable load reduction, indicating resource responsiveness.']
  settlement_amount_usd decimal(15,2) [note: 'The calculated payment amount in US dollars owed to the resource for its DR performance in this event, based on contracted rates and actual reduction.']
  settlement_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the financial settlement process for this resource response.']
  telemetry_quality_flag varchar [note: 'Data quality indicator for the metered telemetry used in this response measurement.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this resource response record was last modified.']
  verification_method varchar [note: 'The method used to verify and validate the resource response performance.']
  weather_adjustment_applied boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a weather-based adjustment was applied to the baseline calculation to account for temperature or other weather impacts.']

  Note: 'Captures the measured performance response of each individual DR resource or aggregator to a specific DR dispatch event. Records resource identifier, nominated MW reduction, actual metered MW reduction, response time, compliance flag, and performance score. Used for DR settlement, program compliance verification, and resource performance tracking.'
}

Table gridops.grid_contingency {
  grid_contingency_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the grid contingency scenario record. Primary key for the grid contingency data product.']
  scada_system_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the SCADA system that provides real-time telemetry data for the elements involved in this contingency scenario.']
  balancing_area_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the balancing area or balancing authority area where this contingency is defined and monitored, used for jurisdictional and operational coordination.']
  cascading_outage_risk varchar [note: 'Assessment of the risk that this contingency could trigger cascading outages affecting a wider area of the Bulk Electric System (BES), based on system topology, protection schemes, and historical events.']
  contingency_category varchar [note: 'NERC TPL planning category classification: P0 (no contingency/base case), P1 (single element), P2 (single element with stuck breaker), P3 (loss of generator), P4 (multiple elements), P5 (delayed fault clearing), P6 (system instability), P7 (common structure). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: P0|P1|P2|P3|P4|P5|P6|P7 — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  contingency_code varchar [note: 'Unique business identifier or code used to reference this contingency in operational systems, study reports, and inter-system communication.']
  contingency_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name or label assigned to this contingency scenario for operator identification and reference in Energy Management System (EMS) displays and reports.']
  contingency_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the contingency scenario based on the number and type of elements removed. N-1 represents single element outage, N-2 represents simultaneous loss of two elements, N-1-1 represents sequential loss of two elements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: N-1|N-2|N-1-1|generator_trip|line_trip|transformer_trip|bus_fault|multiple_element — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  corrective_action_required boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether corrective actions (generation redispatch, transmission switching, load shedding) are required to maintain system reliability if this contingency occurs.']
  corrective_action_time_minutes varchar [note: 'Maximum time in minutes allowed to implement corrective actions after this contingency occurs, based on thermal time constants, voltage decay rates, and operational procedures.']
  corrective_action_type varchar [note: 'Type of corrective action recommended or required to mitigate violations resulting from this contingency. May include multiple actions separated by semicolons (e.g., \'generation redispatch; transmission switching\').']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this contingency record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.']
  dms_zone_code varchar [note: 'Identifier linking this contingency to the DMS zone for transmission-distribution coordination and voltage control at the interface.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this contingency definition became active and was included in security assessment processes.']
  elements_removed_count varchar [note: 'Count of transmission or generation elements (lines, transformers, generators, buses) that are removed or tripped in this contingency scenario definition.']
  ems_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the EMS system instance where this contingency definition is maintained and where real-time security assessments are executed.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'Date when this contingency definition expires or is scheduled to be removed from active security assessment, typically due to system topology changes or element retirement. Null for indefinite contingencies.']
  geographic_region varchar [note: 'Geographic region or sub-region identifier for this contingency, used for regional reliability coordination and reporting.']
  grid_contingency_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the contingency scenario in the real-time security assessment engine. Active contingencies are monitored continuously; inactive contingencies are excluded from real-time analysis.']
  interconnection_type varchar [note: 'North American power grid interconnection where this contingency is located: Eastern Interconnection, Western Interconnection, Texas Interconnection (ERCOT), or Quebec Interconnection.']
  last_assessment_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent real-time or study-mode security assessment execution that evaluated this contingency scenario.']
  last_violation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this contingency most recently resulted in a thermal, voltage, or stability violation during security assessment. Null if no violations have been detected.']
  load_at_risk_mw decimal(12,2) [note: 'Total customer load in megawatts that could be interrupted or at risk of interruption if this contingency occurs and results in cascading outages or system instability.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this contingency record was most recently modified, supporting change tracking and audit requirements.']
  monitoring_elements_count varchar [note: 'Count of transmission elements (lines, transformers, interfaces) that are monitored for thermal overload, voltage violation, or stability issues when this contingency is applied in security assessment.']
  nerc_cip_classification varchar [note: 'NERC CIP impact rating classification for the elements involved in this contingency, indicating the cyber security and physical security requirements applicable to these assets.']
  nerc_region varchar [note: 'NERC regional entity with reliability oversight for this contingency scenario (e.g., WECC, MRO, NPCC, RF, SERC, Texas RE).']
  oms_zone_code varchar [note: 'Identifier linking this contingency to the OMS zone for coordination of planned and unplanned outage management and customer impact assessment.']
  primary_element_name varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the primary transmission or generation element that is removed in this contingency scenario, as defined in the EMS network model.']
  primary_element_type varchar [note: 'Type classification of the primary element that is removed or fails in this contingency scenario.']
  primary_element_voltage_kv decimal(10,2) [note: 'Nominal voltage level in kilovolts of the primary element involved in the contingency scenario.']
  probability_class varchar [note: 'Qualitative assessment of the likelihood of this contingency occurring based on historical outage data, equipment reliability, and operational experience.']
  probability_value decimal(10,6) [note: 'Quantitative probability estimate (0.0 to 1.0) representing the annual likelihood of this contingency scenario occurring, derived from historical reliability data and risk assessment models.']
  real_time_assessment_enabled boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this contingency is included in the real-time security assessment (RTSA) engine that runs continuously in the EMS to monitor system security.']
  rto_iso_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the RTO or ISO that has operational or planning jurisdiction over this contingency scenario (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE).']
  secondary_element_name varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the secondary element removed in N-2 or N-1-1 contingency scenarios. Null for single-element contingencies.']
  secondary_element_type varchar [note: 'Type classification of the secondary element removed in N-2 or N-1-1 contingency scenarios. Set to \'none\' for single-element (N-1) contingencies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: transmission_line|transformer|generator|bus|shunt_device|hvdc_link|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  severity_rating varchar [note: 'Assessment of the potential impact severity if this contingency were to occur, considering load at risk, voltage collapse potential, cascading outage risk, and system stability margin degradation.']
  stability_margin_percent decimal(6,2) [note: 'Percentage margin between the current operating point and the stability limit (voltage collapse point or transient stability limit) under this contingency scenario. Higher values indicate greater system security.']
  state_code varchar [note: 'Two-letter state or province code where the primary contingency element is located, used for regulatory reporting and jurisdictional coordination.']
  study_mode_enabled boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this contingency is included in offline study-mode security assessments used for day-ahead planning, seasonal studies, and long-term transmission planning.']
  thermal_limit_mva decimal(12,2) [note: 'Maximum thermal capacity in MVA for the most critical monitored element under this contingency scenario, representing the binding constraint for system operations.']
  voltage_limit_lower_pu decimal(6,4) [note: 'Minimum acceptable voltage in per-unit (pu) for monitored buses under this contingency scenario, typically 0.90 to 0.95 pu for transmission systems per NERC standards.']
  voltage_limit_upper_pu decimal(6,4) [note: 'Maximum acceptable voltage in per-unit (pu) for monitored buses under this contingency scenario, typically 1.05 to 1.10 pu for transmission systems per NERC standards.']

  Note: 'Defines credible contingency scenarios (N-1, N-2, N-1-1) and stores all real-time and study-mode security assessment results performed by the EMS. Master contingency records specify contingency name, element(s) removed, contingency type, probability, monitoring elements, thermal and voltage limits, and active/inactive status in real-time security assessment. Assessment result records capture study timestamp, study type (real-time, day-ahead, planning), base case power flow results, number of violations found, worst-case contingency ranking, thermal overload details, voltage violation details, stability margin, and recommended corrective actions (redispatch, switching, load shed). Supports NERC TPL-001 through TPL-004, FAC-001/FAC-002 reliability standards, operator situational awareness, and real-time reliability compliance.'
}

Table gridops.security_assessment {
