  security_assessment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the security assessment record. Primary key.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the balancing area under which this security assessment was conducted.']
  control_zone_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the control zone where this security assessment was performed.']
  grid_contingency_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the contingency that resulted in the most severe violations or highest risk during this assessment.']
  assessment_duration_seconds varchar [note: 'Total execution time of the security assessment in seconds, from initiation to completion.']
  assessment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the security assessment execution: completed (successfully finished), in-progress (currently running), failed (error during execution), aborted (manually stopped), or pending-review (awaiting operator validation).']
  assessment_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the security assessment was executed by the Energy Management System (EMS). This is the principal business event timestamp for the assessment.']
  assessment_type varchar [note: 'The type of security assessment performed: real-time (operational), study-mode (what-if analysis), post-contingency (after event), pre-contingency (preventive), seasonal (long-term planning), or planning (future scenario).']
  contingency_count varchar [note: 'Total number of contingencies (N-1, N-2, etc.) analyzed during this security assessment.']
  convergence_iterations varchar [note: 'Number of iterations required for the power flow calculation to converge during the assessment.']
  corrective_action_required boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether corrective actions are required to resolve violations identified in this assessment (True = corrective actions needed, False = no actions needed).']
  corrective_action_summary varchar [note: 'Summary of recommended corrective actions to address violations, such as generation redispatch, load shedding, switching operations, or voltage control adjustments.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this security assessment record was first created in the system.']
  ems_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the Energy Management System (EMS) that performed this security assessment.']
  max_thermal_loading_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The highest thermal loading percentage observed on any transmission element during the assessment, expressed as a percentage of the element\'s rated capacity.']
  max_voltage_pu decimal(6,4) [note: 'The highest voltage level observed at any bus during the assessment, expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage.']
  min_voltage_pu decimal(6,4) [note: 'The lowest voltage level observed at any bus during the assessment, expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this security assessment record was last modified or updated.']
  nerc_compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the assessment results meet NERC reliability compliance requirements (True = compliant, False = non-compliant).']
  notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the Reliability Coordinator or other stakeholders were notified of critical assessment results.']
  operator_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes entered by the system operator regarding the assessment results, actions taken, or special conditions observed.']
  peak_demand_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the assessment was performed during a peak demand period (True = peak demand, False = off-peak).']
  power_flow_convergence_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the power flow calculation converged successfully during the assessment (True = converged, False = did not converge).']
  reliability_coordinator_notified boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the Reliability Coordinator was notified of critical violations found in this assessment (True = notified, False = not notified).']
  reserve_margin_mw decimal(10,2) [note: 'Available operating reserve margin in megawatts at the time of the assessment, representing the difference between available generation and current load.']
  scada_snapshot_reference varchar [note: 'Identifier of the SCADA data snapshot used as the base case for this security assessment.']
  season varchar [note: 'The season during which the security assessment was performed: winter, spring, summer, or fall. Seasonal conditions impact load patterns and generation availability.']
  stability_violation_count varchar [note: 'Number of stability violations (transient, voltage, or oscillatory stability) detected during dynamic security assessment.']
  study_case_name varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the study case or scenario used for this assessment, typically defined in the EMS study environment.']
  thermal_overload_count varchar [note: 'Number of thermal overload violations detected on transmission lines, transformers, or other equipment during the assessment.']
  total_generation_mw decimal(12,2) [note: 'Total system generation in megawatts at the time of the security assessment.']
  total_load_mw decimal(12,2) [note: 'Total system load in megawatts at the time of the security assessment.']
  violation_count varchar [note: 'Total number of reliability violations (thermal, voltage, stability) detected across all contingencies in this assessment.']
  voltage_violation_count varchar [note: 'Number of voltage limit violations (high or low voltage) detected at buses or substations during the assessment.']
  weather_condition varchar [note: 'Weather condition at the time of the assessment that may impact system reliability: normal, extreme-heat, extreme-cold, high-wind, storm, ice, or fog. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: normal|extreme-heat|extreme-cold|high-wind|storm|ice|fog — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  worst_contingency_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the worst-case contingency scenario, including affected equipment and outage conditions.']
  worst_violation_severity varchar [note: 'Severity classification of the most critical violation found during the assessment: critical (immediate action required), high (urgent attention), medium (monitor closely), low (minor concern), or none (no violations).']

  Note: 'Records results of real-time and study-mode security assessments (contingency analysis, power flow, voltage stability) performed by the EMS. Captures assessment timestamp, study type, number of violations found, worst-case contingency, thermal overload count, voltage violation count, and recommended corrective actions. Supports operator situational awareness and NERC reliability compliance.'
}

Table gridops.operator_log {
  operator_log_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each operator log entry in the grid operations control room. Primary key for the operator_log data product.']
  alarm_event_id varchar [note: 'The alarm identifier from the SCADA or EMS system that triggered or is associated with this log entry. Populated for alarm_acknowledgment entry types. Enables traceability from the operator log back to the originating SCADA alarm in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn.']
  asset_registry_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the primary grid asset (substation, transformer, feeder, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this log entry. Links to the asset management master record in Maximo EAM. Null if the entry is not asset-specific.']
  control_zone_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the grid control zone or balancing area associated with this log entry. Links to the gridops.control_zone master record for geographic and operational context.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the licensed control room operator who authored this log entry. Links to the workforce/employee master record. Required for NERC CIP personnel accountability and shift responsibility tracking.']
  primary_operator_person_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the licensed control room operator who authored this log entry. Links to the workforce/employee master record. Required for NERC CIP personnel accountability and shift responsibility tracking.']
  registry_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the primary grid asset (substation, transformer, feeder, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this log entry. Links to the asset management master record in Maximo EAM. Null if the entry is not asset-specific.']
  reliability_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to a NERC reliability event or OMS outage event that this log entry is associated with. Null if the entry is not tied to a specific reliability event. Enables correlation of operator actions to event timelines.']
  safety_audit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.safety_audit. Business justification: Safety audits review operator logs to verify compliance with operating procedures and identify violations.']
  scada_alarm_alarm_event_id varchar [note: 'The alarm identifier from the SCADA or EMS system that triggered or is associated with this log entry. Populated for alarm_acknowledgment entry types. Enables traceability from the operator log back to the originating SCADA alarm in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn.']
  scada_point_id varchar [note: 'The SCADA data point or tag identifier from OSIsoft PI Historian associated with the measurement or control action referenced in this log entry. Enables direct linkage to real-time operational data for post-event analysis.']
  shift_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the operational shift during which this log entry was created. Enables shift-level aggregation of events, handover documentation, and accountability reporting.']
  shift_supervisor_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the shift supervisor who reviewed or approved this log entry. Required for entries of critical or high priority. Supports supervisory accountability and NERC CIP-004 personnel management compliance.']
  ace_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The Area Control Error (ACE) value in Megawatts (MW) recorded at the time of the log entry. ACE is the real-time difference between actual and scheduled interchange, adjusted for frequency deviation. Critical metric for balancing area control and NERC BAL-001 compliance.']
  ambient_temperature_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Ambient air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the time of the log entry. Relevant for thermal loading analysis, equipment derating, and weather-related event context.']
  approved_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this log entry was formally approved as part of the official operational record. Null if not yet approved. Required for regulatory audit trail integrity.']
  asset_identifier varchar [note: 'Human-readable asset identifier or tag number (e.g., substation name, feeder ID, equipment tag) as recorded by the operator at time of entry. Preserved as entered to maintain the original operational record even if the asset master record changes.']
  asset_type varchar [note: 'Type classification of the grid asset referenced in this log entry. Supports asset-type-specific filtering and analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: substation|transformer|feeder|generator|transmission_line|bus|breaker|capacitor_bank|relay|meter — promote to reference product]']
  attachment_reference varchar [note: 'File path, document management system reference, or URL pointing to supporting documentation attached to this log entry (e.g., switching order PDF, alarm printout, event report). Null if no attachment.']
  cip_classification varchar [note: 'NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) impact classification of the asset or action referenced in this log entry. Determines the level of cybersecurity and physical security controls applicable. Required for NERC CIP-002 asset categorization compliance.']
  communication_method varchar [note: 'The method or channel used for the communication recorded in this log entry. Relevant for NERC COM-001 compliance which mandates reliable communication facilities for grid operators.']
  communication_party varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the external or internal party involved in a communication log entry (e.g., RTO/ISO operator name, neighboring utility, field crew ID, supervisor name). Populated for communication entry types.']
  corrective_action_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this log entry requires a follow-up corrective action, work order, or remediation activity. True = a corrective action has been identified and must be tracked. Supports NERC CIP corrective action plan (CAP) tracking.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this log record was first persisted in the data platform (Silver layer). Distinct from entry_timestamp (when the operator created the entry) and event_occurred_timestamp (when the event happened). Used for data lineage and audit trail.']
  dr_dispatch_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The quantity of Demand Response (DR) capacity dispatched or curtailed in Megawatts (MW) as recorded in this log entry. Populated for demand_response entry category entries.']
  entry_category varchar [note: 'Operational category classifying the functional area of the grid operation described in this log entry. Supports domain-specific filtering for post-event analysis and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation|transmission|distribution|demand_response|frequency_regulation|voltage_control|outage|switching|environmental|safety|administrative — promote to reference product]']
  entry_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the log entry within the control room logging workflow. \'draft\' = in progress; \'submitted\' = finalized by operator; \'reviewed\' = reviewed by shift supervisor; \'approved\' = approved for official record; \'voided\' = invalidated with reason.']
  entry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (UTC) when the operator created or submitted the log entry in the Energy Management System (EMS) or control room logging system. This is the principal real-world event time for the log record. Conforms to yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.']
  entry_type varchar [note: 'Categorical discriminator classifying the nature of the log entry. \'action\' = operator-initiated grid action; \'alarm_acknowledgment\' = SCADA/EMS alarm acknowledged; \'communication\' = inter-operator or inter-entity communication; \'observation\' = operational observation or reading; \'switching_order\' = switching order execution step; \'note\' = general operational note.']
  event_occurred_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (UTC) when the actual grid event, alarm, or operational action physically occurred, as distinct from when the operator recorded it. Critical for post-event timeline reconstruction and NERC reliability event analysis. May differ from entry_timestamp due to logging latency.']
  frequency_hz decimal(8,4) [note: 'The measured system frequency in Hertz (Hz) at the time of the log entry, as recorded by the operator or captured from SCADA. Relevant for frequency regulation events and under-frequency load shedding actions. Nominal value is 60.0000 Hz for North American grids.']
  generation_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The measured or dispatched generation output in Megawatts (MW) referenced in this log entry. Relevant for generation dispatch, curtailment, and unit commitment actions.']
  load_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'The measured or observed load in Megawatts (MW) at the time of the log entry. Relevant for load shedding, demand response dispatch, and load balancing actions. Null if not applicable to the entry type.']
  log_entry_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable sequential identifier for the log entry (e.g., OL-2024-00123456). Used for cross-referencing in regulatory audits, NERC compliance filings, and post-event analysis reports.']
  narrative varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative entered by the operator describing the action taken, observation made, alarm acknowledged, or communication recorded. This is the primary payload of the log entry and serves as the official operational record for post-event analysis, regulatory audits, and NERC CIP compliance reviews.']
  nerc_reportable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this log entry is associated with a NERC-reportable reliability event per NERC EOP-004 disturbance reporting thresholds. True = event meets NERC reporting criteria and must be submitted to NERC/DOE via OE-417 or similar form.']
  nerc_standard_reference varchar [note: 'The specific NERC Reliability Standard(s) applicable to the action or event described in this log entry (e.g., BAL-001, EOP-004, CIP-007). Supports compliance mapping and regulatory audit traceability.']
  outage_ticket_number varchar [note: 'The outage ticket or trouble order number from the OMS associated with this log entry. Populated when the log entry relates to an active outage event. Enables correlation between operator actions and outage management workflows.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'Operational priority or severity level assigned to the log entry, indicating urgency and potential grid impact. \'critical\' entries typically correspond to NERC reportable events or imminent reliability threats.']
  puc_reportable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this log entry is associated with an event that must be reported to the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Public Service Commission (PSC) per state regulatory requirements. True = state regulatory reporting obligation exists.']
  reviewed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the shift supervisor reviewed this log entry. Null if not yet reviewed. Part of the log entry lifecycle audit trail required for NERC compliance.']
  source_log_reference varchar [note: 'The native log or record identifier from the originating source system (EMS, DMS, OMS, SCADA). Enables traceability back to the system of record for data lineage and reconciliation purposes in the Silver layer.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The originating operational system from which this log entry was generated or ingested. \'ems\' = Energy Management System; \'dms\' = Distribution Management System; \'oms\' = Outage Management System; \'scada\' = SCADA system; \'pi_historian\' = OSIsoft PI Historian; \'manual\' = manually entered by operator.']
  switching_order_number varchar [note: 'The switching order number from the DMS/OMS system associated with this log entry. Populated for switching_order entry types. Links the operator log to the formal switching order workflow in GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this log record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks amendments, supervisor reviews, and status transitions. Required for Silver layer change data capture and audit trail completeness.']
  void_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation for why this log entry was voided or invalidated. Populated only when entry_status = \'voided\'. Maintains audit trail integrity by preserving the reason for invalidation rather than deleting the record.']
  voltage_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'The measured or observed voltage in kilovolts (kV) at the referenced asset or bus at the time of the log entry. Relevant for voltage control actions, voltage deviation events, and reactive power dispatch entries.']
  weather_condition varchar [note: 'Prevailing weather condition at the time of the log entry as observed or reported by the operator. Relevant for weather-related outage events, load forecasting context, and post-event causal analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|cloudy|rain|thunderstorm|snow|ice|high_wind|fog|extreme_heat — promote to reference product]']
  work_order_number varchar [note: 'The Maximo EAM work order number associated with corrective or maintenance actions triggered by this log entry. Populated when corrective_action_required = True. Enables traceability from operational events to maintenance work execution.']

  Note: 'Chronological log of operator actions, observations, and communications recorded in the grid operations control room. Each entry captures timestamp, operator ID, shift, log entry type (action, alarm acknowledgment, communication, note), associated asset or event, and free-text narrative. Serves as the official operational record for post-event analysis, regulatory audits, and NERC CIP compliance.'
}

Table gridops.alarm_event {
  alarm_event_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the alarm event record. Primary key.']
  asset_registry_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the physical grid asset (transformer, breaker, line, generator, etc.) associated with this alarm. Links to the enterprise asset management system.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the NERC-registered balancing area where the alarm occurred. Links to the gridops.balancing_area product.']
  control_zone_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the control zone or dispatch area responsible for this alarm. Links to the gridops.control_zone product.']
  distribution_switching_order_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the switching order associated with this alarm if the alarm was triggered during planned switching operations. Links to gridops.switching_order.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'User ID or employee number of the operator who acknowledged the alarm. Used for performance tracking and audit trails.']
  gridops_outage_event_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the associated outage event if this alarm is related to a customer outage or system disturbance. Links to the OMS (Outage Management System).']
  registry_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the physical grid asset (transformer, breaker, line, generator, etc.) associated with this alarm. Links to the enterprise asset management system.']
  scada_point_id varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the SCADA point or tag that generated this alarm. Links to the monitored asset or measurement point in the SCADA system.']
  shelved_by_operator_employee_id varchar [note: 'User ID of the operator who shelved the alarm. Required for audit and compliance.']
  transmission_substation_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the substation where the alarmed asset is located. Null for transmission line or distributed asset alarms.']
  work_order_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the maintenance or repair work order created in response to this alarm. Links to the EAM (Enterprise Asset Management) system.']
  acknowledged_by_operator_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the operator who acknowledged the alarm. Denormalized for reporting convenience.']
  acknowledged_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the alarm has been acknowledged by an operator. True if acknowledged, False if still unacknowledged.']
  acknowledged_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the alarm was acknowledged by an operator. Null if not yet acknowledged.']
  alarm_category varchar [note: 'Business classification of the alarm condition: thermal_overload (conductor or transformer heating), voltage_violation (over/under voltage), frequency_deviation (grid frequency out of range), equipment_failure (device malfunction), communication_loss (telemetry failure), or protection_system (relay or breaker operation).']
  alarm_count varchar [note: 'Number of times this alarm condition has occurred for this asset within the current analysis window. Used for alarm flood detection and nuisance alarm identification.']
  alarm_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the alarm condition, including context, potential causes, and recommended operator actions. Used for training and alarm rationalization.']
  alarm_message varchar [note: 'Full alarm message text as presented to the operator in the SCADA/EMS system. Includes asset name, condition description, and measured value.']
  alarm_state varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the alarm: active (unacknowledged and condition persists), acknowledged (operator has seen it), cleared (condition returned to normal), shelved (temporarily disabled), suppressed (filtered by alarm management logic), or stale (communication lost).']
  alarm_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time when the alarm condition was detected and the alarm was triggered in the SCADA/EMS system. This is the operational event time, distinct from record creation time.']
  alarm_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the alarm based on the nature of the monitored condition: analog (threshold violation on continuous measurement), digital (discrete state change), calculated (derived condition), communication (loss of signal), equipment_status (device health), or protection_operation (relay trip).']
  cip_classification varchar [note: 'NERC CIP impact classification of the asset or system that generated this alarm: high (critical cyber assets), medium (medium impact BES cyber systems), low (low impact BES cyber systems), or not_applicable.']
  cleared_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the alarm condition returned to normal and the alarm was cleared. Null if alarm is still active.']
  ems_alarm_code varchar [note: 'Native alarm identifier from the EMS system. Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trails.']
  gis_feature_reference varchar [note: 'Identifier of the GIS feature (point, line, polygon) representing the alarmed asset in the enterprise GIS system. Enables spatial analysis and map visualization.']
  latitude decimal(10,7) [note: 'Geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees) of the alarmed asset location. Used for spatial analysis and mobile workforce dispatch.']
  longitude decimal(10,7) [note: 'Geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees) of the alarmed asset location. Used for spatial analysis and mobile workforce dispatch.']
  nerc_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this alarm represents a condition that must be reported to NERC under reliability standards (e.g., Bulk Electric System disturbance, CIP cyber security event). True if reportable, False otherwise.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'Operator response priority assigned to the alarm per ISA-18.2 alarm rationalization methodology. Critical alarms require immediate action; informational alarms are for awareness only.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this alarm event record was first inserted into the data platform. Distinct from alarm_timestamp (operational event time). Used for data lineage and audit.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this alarm event record was last modified in the data platform. Updated when alarm state changes (acknowledged, cleared, shelved).']
  shelved_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the alarm has been temporarily shelved (suppressed) by an operator. True if shelved, False otherwise. Shelving is used during maintenance or known abnormal conditions.']
  shelved_reason varchar [note: 'Operator-entered justification for shelving the alarm (e.g., \'Planned maintenance on Transformer T-101\', \'Known communication issue during storm\').']
  shelved_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the alarm was shelved. Null if not shelved.']
  suppressed_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the alarm was automatically suppressed by alarm management logic (e.g., flood suppression, consequential alarm filtering). True if suppressed, False otherwise.']
  suppression_rule varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the alarm management rule that suppressed this alarm (e.g., \'Substation Lockout Flood Suppression\', \'Communication Loss Consequential Filter\').']
  threshold_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The configured threshold or setpoint that was exceeded to trigger the alarm (e.g., high limit, low limit, deadband). Null for digital/status alarms.']
  time_to_acknowledge_seconds varchar [note: 'Elapsed time in seconds between alarm_timestamp and acknowledged_timestamp. Key performance indicator for operator response time per ISA-18.2.']
  time_to_clear_seconds varchar [note: 'Elapsed time in seconds between alarm_timestamp and cleared_timestamp. Measures total alarm duration and system restoration time.']
  trigger_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'The measured value that triggered the alarm condition (e.g., actual current in amps, voltage in kV, temperature in Celsius, frequency in Hz). Null for digital/status alarms.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Engineering unit for the trigger_value and threshold_value fields (e.g., \'A\' for amps, \'kV\' for kilovolts, \'MW\' for megawatts, \'Hz\' for hertz, \'C\' for Celsius, \'psi\' for pressure).']
  voltage_level_kv decimal(10,2) [note: 'Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the circuit or equipment where the alarm occurred (e.g., 345, 138, 69, 13.8, 4.16).']

  Note: 'Records each SCADA/EMS alarm generated from monitored grid assets including thermal overloads, voltage violations, equipment failures, communication loss, and protection system operations. Captures alarm point, alarm type, priority level (per ISA-18.2 alarm management standard), trigger value, threshold, acknowledgment status, acknowledging operator, shelving status, and time to acknowledge/clear. Supports alarm rationalization, operator performance review, and NERC CIP-007 compliance.'
}

Table gridops.energy_balance {
  energy_balance_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each energy balance record in the balancing area. Primary key for the energy_balance data product.']
  aggregation_group_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to der.aggregation_group. Business justification: Energy balance reports are broken out by aggregation groups for market settlement and DER performance analysis.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the NERC-registered Balancing Authority Area (BAA) for which this energy balance record applies. Links to the balancing_area master record.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the system operator or EMS user responsible for reviewing or manually adjusting this energy balance record. Populated for manual entries or operator-confirmed revisions. Links to workforce/operator master data.']
  gl_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Energy Balance records are posted to the General Ledger for financial statements and regulatory filings.']
  person_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the system operator or EMS user responsible for reviewing or manually adjusting this energy balance record. Populated for manual entries or operator-confirmed revisions. Links to workforce/operator master data.']
  product_rate_schedule_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.rate_schedule. Business justification: Settlement report requires applying the correct rate schedule to each balancing area energy balance for billing compliance.']
  regulatory_rate_case_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Energy balance statements are submitted as part of rate‑case settlements; linking provides traceability to the specific rate case.']
  ace_average_mw decimal(18,6) [note: 'Average Area Control Error (ACE) over the interval period in Megawatts (MW). Used for NERC Control Performance Standard (CPS1/CPS2) compliance calculations and regulatory reporting to NERC and state PUCs.']
  ace_mw decimal(18,6) [note: 'Area Control Error (ACE) for the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatts (MW). ACE = (Actual Net Interchange – Scheduled Net Interchange) – 10B(Actual Frequency – Scheduled Frequency). Key NERC BAL-001 compliance metric measuring real-time generation-load balance.']
  actual_interchange_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Actual metered energy interchange across balancing area tie-lines during the interval, expressed in MWh. Compared against scheduled_interchange_mwh to compute interchange deviation for NERC BAL compliance.']
  cps1_score decimal(8,4) [note: 'NERC Control Performance Standard 1 (CPS1) compliance score for the interval, expressed as a percentage. CPS1 measures the one-minute average ACE relative to frequency deviation. NERC requires a minimum 100% CPS1 score on a rolling 12-month basis.']
  cps2_violation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the balancing area exceeded the NERC Control Performance Standard 2 (CPS2) ACE limit (L10) during this interval. True = CPS2 violation occurred; False = within limits. Triggers mandatory NERC reporting when True.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this energy balance record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse, typically upon ingestion from SCADA/PI Historian or EMS. Audit trail field for data lineage.']
  data_quality_code varchar [note: 'Quality indicator for the energy balance record derived from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry quality flags. \'good\' = validated telemetry; \'suspect\' = questionable reading requiring review; \'estimated\' = gap-filled or interpolated; \'bad\' = failed quality check; \'missing\' = no telemetry received.']
  data_source varchar [note: 'Identifies the primary source system from which this energy balance record was derived. \'scada\' = GE PowerOn SCADA telemetry; \'pi_historian\' = OSIsoft PI Historian; \'ems\' = Energy Management System calculated; \'manual\' = operator-entered; \'estimated\' = gap-filled estimate.']
  der_net_injection_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Net energy injected into the grid from Distributed Energy Resources (DER) including rooftop solar, battery storage, and small-scale generation during the interval, expressed in MWh. Tracked via DERMS integration.']
  dr_response_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Energy reduction achieved through Demand Response (DR) dispatch during the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents load curtailment from DR programs activated by the EMS/DERMS. Used for DR settlement and NERC BAL compliance.']
  eia_930_reported_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this energy balance record has been included in an EIA Form 930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor) submission. True = reported to EIA; False = pending submission. Supports regulatory reporting completeness tracking.']
  eia_ba_code varchar [note: 'EIA-assigned balancing authority code for the reporting entity. Required for EIA Form 930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor) submission. Uniquely identifies the balancing authority in EIA\'s national energy data system.']
  finalized_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this energy balance record was promoted from \'preliminary\' to \'final\' status following validation. Marks the completion of the operational accounting close for the interval.']
  fossil_generation_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Total energy generated from fossil fuel sources (natural gas, coal, oil) within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Used for emissions reporting to EPA and EIA.']
  frequency_bias_mw_per_hz decimal(12,4) [note: 'The frequency bias setting (B) applied in the ACE calculation formula for this interval, expressed in MW/Hz. Represents the balancing area\'s contribution to primary frequency response. Filed annually with NERC.']
  frequency_hz decimal(10,6) [note: 'Average system frequency measured in Hertz (Hz) during the interval. Nominal value is 60.000 Hz for the North American interconnection. Deviations from nominal drive ACE calculations and frequency regulation dispatch.']
  inadvertent_interchange_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Accumulated inadvertent energy interchange for the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents the difference between actual and scheduled interchange that must be repaid to neighboring balancing areas per NERC BAL-005 payback requirements.']
  interconnection varchar [note: 'North American electrical interconnection to which this balancing area belongs. Determines synchronous frequency reference and reliability coordinator jurisdiction.']
  interval_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Duration of the energy balance interval in minutes (e.g., 5, 15, 30, 60). Distinguishes sub-hourly from hourly records and supports aggregation logic.']
  interval_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The ending timestamp of the energy accounting interval. Together with interval_start_timestamp defines the precise measurement window for this balance record.']
  interval_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The beginning timestamp of the energy accounting interval (hourly or sub-hourly) for which this balance record is computed. Derived from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry. Conforms to ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  load_forecast_error_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Difference between actual total load and forecasted load for the interval, expressed in MWh (actual minus forecast). Positive value indicates load exceeded forecast; negative indicates load was below forecast. Used to evaluate forecasting accuracy and improve EMS models.']
  load_forecast_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Forecasted energy load for the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Generated by the EMS load forecasting module prior to the operating interval. Used to compute forecast error and support dispatch planning.']
  nerc_compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this energy balance interval is fully compliant with applicable NERC BAL reliability standards (BAL-001, BAL-002, BAL-003, BAL-005). True = compliant; False = one or more NERC BAL standard violations detected. Triggers compliance workflow when False.']
  nerc_tag_number varchar [note: 'NERC e-Tag identifier associated with the scheduled interchange transactions contributing to this energy balance interval. Used for cross-referencing with NERC e-Tag system for interchange scheduling and curtailment tracking.']
  net_interchange_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Net energy exchanged across the balancing area boundary during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Positive value indicates net export; negative value indicates net import. Computed as sum of all scheduled and actual tie-line flows.']
  nuclear_generation_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Total energy generated from nuclear sources within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Reported separately per NRC and EIA requirements.']
  operating_date date [note: 'The calendar date (in local prevailing time) to which this energy balance interval belongs. Used for daily aggregation, settlement, and regulatory reporting aligned to the operating day.']
  operating_hour varchar [note: 'The hour of the operating day (0–23) in which this interval falls, expressed in local prevailing time. Used for hourly aggregation, TOU analysis, and RTO/ISO settlement hour alignment.']
  operating_reserve_mw decimal(12,4) [note: 'Total operating reserve available in the balancing area at the start of the interval, expressed in Megawatts (MW). Includes spinning and non-spinning reserves. NERC BAL-002 compliance metric.']
  record_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of the energy balance record indicating its processing and settlement state. \'preliminary\' = near-real-time estimate; \'final\' = validated operational accounting; \'revised\' = corrected after initial finalization; \'settled\' = accepted by RTO/ISO for financial settlement; \'void\' = invalidated record.']
  renewable_generation_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Total energy generated from renewable sources (wind, solar, hydro, geothermal, biomass) within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Supports Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) tracking and IRP reporting.']
  revision_number varchar [note: 'Sequential revision counter for this energy balance record. Starts at 0 for the initial preliminary record and increments with each correction or resettlement. Supports audit trail and version management for regulatory submissions.']
  revision_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the reason for the most recent revision to this energy balance record (e.g., \'meter data correction\', \'SCADA telemetry gap fill\', \'RTO settlement adjustment\'). Populated only when revision_number > 0.']
  rto_iso_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) with which this balancing area is affiliated for market settlement and reliability coordination (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE).']
  scheduled_interchange_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Total energy interchange scheduled across balancing area tie-lines for the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) or intra-day scheduled position prior to real-time deviations.']
  settled_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this energy balance record was accepted and confirmed by the RTO/ISO for financial settlement. Marks the completion of the market settlement lifecycle for the interval.']
  settlement_period_type varchar [note: 'Identifies the market settlement period type for this energy balance record. \'real_time\' = RTM interval data; \'day_ahead\' = DAM scheduled position; \'final_settlement\' = post-operating-day settlement; \'resettlement\' = corrected settlement after dispute resolution.']
  spinning_reserve_mw decimal(12,4) [note: 'Spinning (synchronized) reserve available in the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MW. Subset of operating_reserve_mw representing generation online and capable of immediate response. NERC BAL-002 compliance metric.']
  total_generation_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Total electrical energy generated within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Aggregates all generation resources including fossil fuel, nuclear, and renewable sources. Sourced from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry.']
  total_load_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Total electrical energy consumed by load within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Represents native load plus losses. Sourced from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry.']
  transmission_losses_mwh decimal(18,6) [note: 'Estimated electrical energy lost in transmission and distribution within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Used in energy accounting identity: Generation = Load + Net Interchange + Losses.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this energy balance record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Updated on each revision, status change, or data quality correction.']

  Note: 'Hourly and sub-hourly energy balance records for the balancing area capturing total generation (MWh), total load (MWh), net interchange (MWh), losses, and ACE (Area Control Error). Derived from SCADA telemetry and used for NERC BAL compliance reporting, settlement with RTOs/ISOs, and operational accounting. Represents the authoritative near-real-time energy accounting record for the balancing area.'
}

Table gridops.transmission_limit {
  transmission_limit_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the transmission limit record. Primary key for this entity.']
  balancing_area_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Transmission limits are defined per balancing area; FK adds relational context.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the transmission engineer or reliability coordinator who approved this limit for operational use.']
  facility_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the transmission facility (line, transformer, flowgate, interface) to which this limit applies.']
  ambient_temperature_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at which the limit rating was calculated. Used for dynamic rating adjustments.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which this transmission limit was formally approved for enforcement in real-time operations.']
  contingency_name varchar [note: 'Name of the contingency scenario (e.g., N-1, N-2 outage) under which this limit applies. Identifies the specific outage condition that triggers this constraint.']
  contingency_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the contingency: N-1 (single element outage), N-2 (double contingency), base case (no outage), or extreme event.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this transmission limit record was first created in the system.']
  dynamic_rating_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether dynamic line rating (real-time adjustment based on weather and conductor temperature) is enabled for this facility. True if enabled, False otherwise.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which this transmission limit becomes active and enforceable in real-time operations and EMS security analysis.']
  emergency_rating_15min_mva decimal(12,3) [note: 'Short-term emergency rating in MVA that the facility can sustain for up to 15 minutes without damage, used during contingency conditions.']
  emergency_rating_4hr_mva decimal(12,3) [note: 'Long-term emergency rating in MVA that the facility can sustain for up to 4 hours, typically used for post-contingency load relief operations.']
  ems_limit_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of this limit record in the Energy Management System (EMS) used for real-time security analysis and dispatch.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'Date on which this transmission limit expires or is superseded by a new limit. Null if the limit is open-ended.']
  ferc_jurisdiction boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this transmission facility and its limits fall under FERC jurisdiction (interstate transmission). True if FERC-jurisdictional, False otherwise.']
  gis_feature_reference varchar [note: 'Identifier of the corresponding transmission facility feature in the GIS system, used for geospatial analysis and mapping.']
  limit_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes providing additional context, operational instructions, or special conditions related to this transmission limit.']
  limit_source varchar [note: 'Origin of the limit value: thermal analysis, voltage analysis, stability study, manufacturer equipment rating, field test measurement, or engineering judgment.']
  limit_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the limit record: active (enforced in EMS), inactive, suspended (temporarily not enforced), pending approval, or retired.']
  limit_type varchar [note: 'Physical constraint type: thermal (conductor heating), voltage (bus voltage deviation), stability (transient/voltage/oscillatory stability limits).']
  load_dump_rating_mva decimal(12,3) [note: 'Maximum load that can be shed or transferred through this facility during emergency load dump or load shedding operations.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this transmission limit record was last modified or updated.']
  nerc_cip_classification varchar [note: 'NERC CIP impact classification of the facility: high, medium, low, or not applicable. Determines cybersecurity and physical security requirements.']
  normal_rating_mva decimal(12,3) [note: 'Continuous normal operating limit in megavolt-amperes (MVA) under normal ambient and system conditions. This is the baseline thermal or transfer capability limit.']
  normal_rating_mw decimal(12,3) [note: 'Continuous normal operating limit in megawatts (MW) for real power transfer. Used for flowgates and interfaces where MW is the primary constraint metric.']
  rto_iso_code varchar [note: 'Code of the RTO or ISO that has operational authority over this transmission facility and enforces these limits in market operations.']
  scada_monitored boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this transmission limit is actively monitored in real-time via SCADA telemetry. True if monitored, False otherwise.']
  season_code varchar [note: 'Season during which this limit applies: summer, winter, spring, fall, or year-round. Seasonal limits reflect ambient temperature and load pattern variations.']
  seasonal_adjustment_factor decimal(5,4) [note: 'Multiplier applied to base ratings to account for seasonal ambient temperature variations (e.g., summer de-rating, winter up-rating). Typically ranges from 0.8 to 1.2.']
  study_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or document name of the engineering study (thermal, voltage, or stability study) that established this limit.']
  voltage_level_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the transmission facility (e.g., 138 kV, 230 kV, 345 kV, 500 kV).']
  voltage_limit_high_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'Upper voltage limit in kilovolts (kV) for voltage-constrained facilities. Exceeding this limit may cause equipment damage or system instability.']
  voltage_limit_low_kv decimal(10,3) [note: 'Lower voltage limit in kilovolts (kV) for voltage-constrained facilities. Falling below this limit may cause voltage collapse or equipment malfunction.']

  Note: 'Master records for thermal, voltage, and stability limits on transmission facilities (lines, transformers, flowgates, interfaces) enforced in real-time operations. Captures normal rating (MVA/MW), emergency rating (15-min/4-hr), load dump rating, seasonal and ambient-adjusted ratings, applicable contingency, limit source (thermal/voltage/stability), and effective date. These limits are the hard constraints enforced by EMS security analysis and operator dispatch decisions per NERC FAC-008.'
}

Table gridops.weather_forecast {

  precipitation_inches decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecasted total precipitation depth in inches.']
  pressure_hpa decimal(7,2) [note: 'Forecasted sea‑level atmospheric pressure in hectopascals.']
  probability_of_precipitation_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecasted likelihood of precipitation expressed as a percentage.']
  record_created_date date [note: 'Calendar date when the forecast record was first stored in the lakehouse.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time of the most recent update to the forecast record.']

  uv_index varchar [note: 'Forecasted ultraviolet index indicating sunburn risk.']
  visibility_mi decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecasted horizontal visibility distance in miles.']
  weather_zone_code varchar [note: 'Standard code identifying the geographic weather zone for the forecast.']
  wind_direction_deg varchar [note: 'Forecasted wind direction expressed as degrees from true north.']
  wind_speed_mph decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecasted wind speed in miles per hour.']

  Note: 'Weather forecast data integrated into grid operations for load forecasting, storm preparation, and renewable generation prediction including temperature, wind speed, cloud cover, and precipitation'
}

Table gridops.dispatch_participation {
  dispatch_participation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the dispatch_participation association']
  dr_dispatch_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to dr_dispatch_event']
  meter_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to meter']
  actual_reduction_mw decimal [note: 'Actual MW reduction achieved by the meter during the dispatch event']
  participation_status varchar [note: 'Status of the meter\'s participation in the dispatch event (e.g., responded, no‑response)']
  response_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the meter reported its response to the dispatch event']

  Note: 'This association product represents the participation of meters in demand‑response dispatch events. Each record links one dr_dispatch_event to one meter and captures attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship.. Existence Justification: A demand‑response dispatch event can involve many meters, and a given meter can be dispatched in many events over time. The utility records each participation with status, actual reduction, and response timestamp, which are attributes of the participation itself. This relationship is actively managed by grid operations and is a distinct business entity.'
}

Table gridops.switching_order_material_allocation {

  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the allocated quantity (e.g., EA, KG)']

  Note: 'Association table that records which material items are allocated to each grid operations switching order, including the quantity, unit of measure, and line status for each material requirement.. Existence Justification: A switching order often requires several spare parts or equipment items, and each material can be used in many different switching orders. The utility tracks the quantity, unit of measure, and status of each material assigned to a specific order, creating a distinct record for every order‑material pair.'
}

Table metering.meter {
  meter_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for meter']
  asset_registry_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: Asset Management process requires linking each physical meter to its asset record for depreciation, work‑order assignment, and compliance reporting.']
  distribution_service_point_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the logical service delivery point representing the utility-customer interconnection. One service point may have multiple meters (e.g., generation and consumption). Used for billing aggregation and rate application.']
  distribution_transformer_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the distribution transformer serving this meter. Used for load balancing, outage analysis, and grid planning. Critical for AMI-based transformer load management and phase identification.']
  gl_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Revenue recognition per meter posts sales to a specific GL account; required for monthly revenue statements.']
  installer_technician_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.technician. Business justification: Installation Process: records which technician installed the meter for warranty, compliance, and asset‑management reporting.']
  it_asset_id varchar [note: 'Unique identifier for the AMI communication endpoint or network interface card attached to or embedded in the meter. Used for network provisioning, firmware updates, and outage detection.']
  location_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the physical installation location of the meter. Links to asset location registry with GPS coordinates, address, and GIS spatial data. Used for field dispatch, outage correlation, and service territory mapping.']
  material_master_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Needed for asset cost tracking and inventory reconciliation, linking each meter to its material master part number.']
  pole_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to distribution.pole. Business justification: Required for field crew maintenance and outage response reports that map each meter to its mounting pole, enabling precise asset location and work order generation.']
  premise_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the service premise (property/building) where the meter is installed. Critical link between metering, billing, and customer systems. Supports multi-meter premises and meter-to-premise history.']
  scada_system_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to technology.scada_system. Business justification: SCADA Integration process assigns each meter to a SCADA system for remote reading and regulatory data submission.']
  vendor_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Required for warranty management and vendor performance reports that tie each installed meter to its supplying vendor.']
  vpp_agreement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to engagement.vpp_agreement. Business justification: VPP Participation Agreements list the meters enrolled for dispatch; regulatory filing mandates explicit meter identifiers.']
  accuracy_class varchar [note: 'ANSI accuracy classification indicating maximum allowable measurement error as a percentage of full scale. Lower numbers indicate higher precision. Determines testing frequency and revenue-grade certification requirements.']
  communication_protocol varchar [note: 'Technical protocol standard used for meter-to-headend communication (e.g., ANSI C12.18, ANSI C12.19, DLMS/COSEM, Zigbee, cellular). Determines data format, security requirements, and system integration approach.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this meter record was first created in the MDM system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and system integration reconciliation. Immutable after initial creation.']
  ct_ratio varchar [note: 'Current transformer ratio for instrument-rated meters (e.g., 200:5, 400:5). Used to calculate actual consumption from meter readings. Null for self-contained meters. Critical for accurate billing calculations.']
  current_rating_amps decimal(10,2) [note: 'Maximum continuous current rating of the electric meter in amperes. Determines meter capacity and must align with service entrance equipment ratings. Used for load analysis and meter sizing validation.']
  demand_metering_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the meter measures and records peak demand (kW) in addition to energy consumption (kWh). Required for commercial/industrial rate structures with demand charges. Determines billing calculation logic.']
  expected_life_years varchar [note: 'Estimated useful life of the meter asset in years for depreciation and replacement planning. Typically 15-30 years depending on technology and service class. Used for capital planning and rate case filings.']
  firmware_version varchar [note: 'Current firmware version installed on the meter device. Critical for security patch management, feature enablement, and compatibility with MDM system. Format varies by manufacturer.']
  form varchar [note: 'ANSI standard form designation indicating meter socket configuration and wiring arrangement (e.g., Form 2S, Form 12S, Form 16S). Determines physical installation requirements and measurement capabilities.']
  installation_date date [note: 'Date the meter was physically installed at the current service location. Used for age analysis, warranty tracking, and lifecycle management. Distinct from manufacturing date.']
  installation_status varchar [note: 'Current physical deployment state of the meter asset. Installed indicates active field deployment. In_stock indicates warehouse inventory. In_shop indicates repair/testing. Retired indicates end-of-life but not yet disposed.']
  last_communication_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of most recent successful data exchange between the meter and the MDM headend system. Used for communication health monitoring, outage detection, and data quality assessment.']
  manufacturer varchar [note: 'Name of the company that manufactured the meter device (e.g., Landis+Gyr, Itron, Sensus, Elster, Aclara). Used for warranty tracking, firmware compatibility, and vendor performance analysis.']
  meter_class varchar [note: 'Customer service class designation for the meter installation. Determines applicable tariffs, demand response eligibility, and regulatory rate class assignment.']
  meter_number varchar [note: 'Manufacturer-assigned serial number stamped on the physical meter device. Externally visible identifier used for field operations, inventory tracking, and regulatory reporting. Must be unique across the service territory.']
  meter_type varchar [note: 'Type of utility commodity measured by this meter device. Determines applicable rate structures, measurement units, and regulatory reporting requirements.']
  model_number varchar [note: 'Manufacturer model designation identifying the specific meter product line and configuration. Used to determine technical specifications, communication protocols, and compatible firmware versions.']
  multiplier decimal(10,4) [note: 'Numeric multiplier applied to meter register readings to calculate actual consumption. Derived from CT/PT ratios and meter configuration. Essential for accurate billing and energy accounting.']
  net_metering_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the meter supports bidirectional energy measurement for customer-owned generation (solar, wind). True for NEM-eligible installations. Requires meter capable of measuring both delivered and received energy.']
  next_test_due_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for next required accuracy test or recertification. Calculated based on last test date and regulatory testing interval. Used for compliance tracking and preventive maintenance scheduling.']
  number_of_dials varchar [note: 'Count of mechanical register dials on the meter face for manual reading. Determines reading format and maximum register capacity. Typically 4-6 dials for residential, more for commercial/industrial.']
  operational_status varchar [note: 'Current operational state indicating whether the meter is actively measuring and reporting consumption. Active meters generate billable reads. Failed meters require replacement. Testing indicates commissioning or troubleshooting.']
  ownership_type varchar [note: 'Legal ownership designation for the meter asset. Utility_owned meters are capitalized assets. Customer_owned meters are tracked for service but not depreciated. Third_party indicates DER or submetering arrangements.']
  pt_ratio varchar [note: 'Potential transformer ratio for high-voltage metering installations (e.g., 7200:120). Used with CT ratio to calculate actual energy consumption. Null for low-voltage self-contained meters.']
  purchase_cost decimal(12,2) [note: 'Original acquisition cost of the meter device in USD. Used for asset capitalization, depreciation calculations, and rate base reporting. Includes device cost only, not installation labor.']
  purchase_date date [note: 'Date the utility acquired the meter from the manufacturer or vendor. Used for warranty tracking, depreciation calculations, and procurement analytics. May differ from installation date.']
  read_cycle varchar [note: 'Billing cycle designation indicating when the meter is read each month (e.g., cycle 01 = 1st-5th of month). Used for billing schedule coordination and read validation. Typically 20-30 cycles per service territory.']
  register_capacity_kwh decimal(15,2) [note: 'Maximum cumulative energy value the meter register can display before rolling over to zero. Used to detect and correct rollover events in consumption calculations. Measured in kilowatt-hours for electric meters.']
  remote_disconnect_capable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the meter has an integrated service switch that can be remotely controlled to connect or disconnect service. Used for credit management, move-in/move-out automation, and emergency load shedding.']
  removal_date date [note: 'Date the meter was removed from service at a premise. Null for currently installed meters. Used for lifecycle tracking, final billing, and asset disposition workflows.']
  route_code varchar [note: 'Geographic route assignment for manual meter reading or field inspection. Used for workforce scheduling and route optimization. May be null for AMI meters with automated reading.']
  seal_number varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the tamper-evident seal applied to the meter enclosure. Used to detect unauthorized access, meter tampering, and theft of service. Recorded during installation and verified during field inspections.']
  test_date date [note: 'Date of most recent accuracy test or calibration performed on the meter. Used to schedule periodic testing per regulatory requirements and manufacturer recommendations. Typically required every 5-15 years depending on jurisdiction.']
  time_of_use_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the meter is configured to collect interval data for time-differentiated rate structures. True for meters supporting TOU, CPP, or RTP rates. Requires AMI technology and MDM interval data processing.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of most recent modification to any field in this meter record. Used for change data capture, downstream system synchronization, and data quality monitoring. Updated automatically on every record change.']
  voltage_class varchar [note: 'Nominal voltage rating for electric meters indicating the electrical service level. Used for safety compliance, meter selection, and grid operations. Primary voltage indicates high-voltage metering with instrument transformers.']
  warranty_expiration_date date [note: 'Date the manufacturer warranty coverage expires. Used to determine repair vs. replace decisions and vendor claim eligibility. Typically 5-10 years from purchase date.']

  Note: 'Master record for every physical meter device deployed across the service territory, covering both electric (AMI/AMR) and gas meters. Stores device identity, manufacturer, model, firmware version, communication module type, meter form factor, voltage class, CT/PT ratios, dial multiplier, number of dials, seal number, AMI endpoint ID, communication protocol (ANSI C12.18/C12.19), installation status, and lifecycle state. Sourced from Oracle Utilities MDM and Maximo EAM. SSOT for meter asset identity in the metering domain.'
}

  regulatory_compliance_flag boolean [note: 'True if the service point meets all applicable regulatory data reporting requirements.']

  service_point_name varchar [note: 'Human‑readable name or label for the service point location.']
  service_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the point provides electric, gas, or both services.']
  service_voltage_kv decimal(5,2) [note: 'Nominal service voltage level in kilovolts.']
  state varchar [note: 'Two‑letter state or province abbreviation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the service point record.']

  Note: 'Master record for each utility service delivery point representing the fixed physical location where energy measurement occurs. Stores service point identifier, service address, GPS coordinates, premise type (residential/commercial/industrial), service voltage level, phase configuration (single/three-phase), distribution transformer reference, feeder reference, gas pressure zone, service type (electric/gas), NEM eligibility flag, and AMI communication attributes (endpoint serial, comm technology, signal strength, last communication timestamp). Unlike meter_premise which tracks which meter is installed where over time, this entity represents the permanent location itself. This is the foundational time-series dataset for TOU, RTP, and CPP rate calculations, load research, and demand analytics. Sourced from AMI head-end systems via OSIsoft PI Historian and loaded into Oracle Utilities MDM. Each record represents one measurement interval for one channel on one meter.'

Table metering.vee_result {
  vee_result_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate key for each Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) processing result record.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the data quality analyst assigned to investigate the issue.']
  meter_id varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the meter asset to which this VEE result applies.']
  register_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the specific register (e.g., total, demand) on the meter that generated the reading.']
  technician_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the data quality analyst assigned to investigate the issue.']
  vee_rule_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to metering.vee_rule. Business justification: vee_result should reference the governing VEE rule via a foreign key; the existing string column is replaced with vee_rule_id.']
  affected_interval_count varchar [note: 'Number of consecutive intervals impacted by the issue.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this VEE result record was first created in the data lake.']
  data_quality_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric score (0‑100) representing overall confidence in the processed value.']
  escalation_level varchar [note: 'Severity level used to determine if the issue requires escalation to higher‑level support.']
  estimation_algorithm varchar [note: 'Algorithm used when the outcome is estimated, describing the method applied.']
  interval_end timestamp [note: 'End time of the measurement interval for which the raw reading was captured.']
  interval_start timestamp [note: 'Start time of the measurement interval for which the raw reading was captured.']
  investigation_notes varchar [note: 'Free‑form notes captured by the analyst during issue investigation.']
  issue_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the last interval affected by the identified issue.']
  issue_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the first interval affected by the identified issue.']
  issue_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the data quality problem detected for the interval.']
  outcome varchar [note: 'Result of the VEE processing: pass, fail, estimated, or edited.']
  override_reason_code varchar [note: 'Code indicating why a manual override or edit was applied to the reading.']
  processed_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Final value after validation, estimation, or editing (may equal raw_value if outcome is pass).']
  processing_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the VEE processing result was generated.']
  raw_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Original unprocessed value reported by the meter for the interval.']
  resolution_action varchar [note: 'Action taken to resolve the data quality issue (e.g., manual edit, algorithmic correction).']
  resolution_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the issue resolution workflow.']
  root_cause_classification varchar [note: 'High‑level categorization of the underlying cause of the data quality issue.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Name of the source system that produced the raw meter reading (e.g., MDM, PI Historian).']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Measurement unit associated with the raw and processed values (e.g., kilowatt‑hour, thousand cubic feet, therm).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this VEE result record.']

  Note: 'Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) processing outcome record and the domain\'s consolidated data quality management entity. Each record represents a VEE processing result for an interval or register read, storing: original raw value, VEE rule applied, validation outcome (pass/fail/estimated/edited), estimation algorithm used (weather-based/similar-day/linear interpolation), edited value, processing timestamp, and override reason code. Also serves as the SSOT for all data quality issue tracking within the metering domain: captures issue type (spike/gap/negative/rollover/communication failure/anomalous consumption/missing reads), affected date range, number of affected intervals, assigned analyst, investigation notes, resolution status, resolution action taken, root cause classification, and escalation history. Supports both automated VEE pipeline outcomes and manual data quality investigation workflows. Core to Oracle Utilities MDM VEE processing, regulatory reporting on estimated bill percentages, and SLA compliance for data completeness.'
}

  rule_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the rule performs validation, estimation, or editing of meter data.']
  rule_version varchar [note: 'Version number of the rule definition, incremented on changes.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Originating system for the rule definition (e.g., Oracle Utilities MDM).']
  threshold_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the threshold value.']
  threshold_value decimal(12,4) [note: 'Numeric threshold used by the rule (e.g., maximum allowed spike magnitude).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the rule record.']
  vee_rule_code varchar [note: 'Business code used to reference the rule in downstream systems.']
  vee_rule_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the rule purpose and logic.']
  vee_rule_name varchar [note: 'Human‑readable name of the VEE rule.']
  vee_rule_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the rule.']

  Note: 'Reference master for VEE validation and estimation rules configured in Oracle Utilities MDM. Stores rule name, rule type (validation/estimation/editing), rule category (spike/gap/negative/rollover/sum-check), threshold parameters, estimation method, applicable commodity (electric/gas), applicable rate class, effective date range, priority order, and active status. Governs the automated data quality processing pipeline for all interval and register read data.'
}

  peak_window_end_time timestamp [note: 'End time of the on‑peak window (HH:MM, 24‑hour).']
  peak_window_start_time timestamp [note: 'Start time of the on‑peak window (HH:MM, 24‑hour).']
  price_multiplier decimal(5,3) [note: 'Factor applied to the base rate for this schedule (e.g., 1.000 for standard, >1 for premium).']
  rate_class varchar [note: 'Customer rate class to which the schedule applies.']
  rtp_interval_mapping varchar [note: 'Length of real‑time pricing intervals that the schedule aligns with.']
  schedule_code varchar [note: 'Business identifier code used in billing and operational systems.']
  schedule_name varchar [note: 'Human‑readable name of the TOU schedule.']
  schedule_type varchar [note: 'Category of the schedule indicating the pricing model.']
  season varchar [note: 'Seasonal grouping that the schedule applies to.']
  tier_definitions varchar [note: 'JSON‑encoded definition of tier periods, start/end times and associated rates within the schedule.']
  time_zone varchar [note: 'IANA time zone identifier for the schedule\'s time windows.']
  tou_schedule_description varchar [note: 'Free‑form text describing the purpose and characteristics of the schedule.']
  tou_schedule_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the schedule.']
  updated_by varchar [note: 'User identifier that performed the last update.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the schedule record.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Incremental version of the schedule for change management.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User identifier that created the schedule record.']

  Note: 'Reference master defining Time-of-Use (TOU) rate period schedules including season definitions (summer/winter/shoulder), day type classifications (weekday/weekend/holiday), on-peak and off-peak time windows, critical peak pricing (CPP) event eligibility windows, and real-time pricing (RTP) interval mappings. Stores schedule code, effective date range, applicable rate class, season start/end months, and tier period definitions. Governs how interval reads are bucketed into TOU tiers for billing determinant calculation.'
}

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the payment record.']

  Note: 'Record of a customer payment transaction applied against outstanding bill balances. Captures payment date, payment method (check, ACH, credit card, cash, auto-pay), payment amount, tender type, payment source channel (web, IVR, walk-in, lockbox), and posting status. Integrates with SAP FI/CO for revenue posting and Oracle CC&B for balance application. SSOT for all customer payment events.'

  billing_rate_component_status varchar [note: 'Operational status indicating whether the component is currently applied to customer bills.']
  calculation_method varchar [note: 'Logic applied to compute the charge (e.g., flat rate, block/tiered, time‑of‑use).']
  component_type varchar [note: 'Category of the component defining its billing purpose (e.g., energy usage, demand charge, fixed customer charge).']

  start_time timestamp [note: 'Clock time when the component\'s interval begins each day.']
  tier_end_quantity decimal(12,4) [note: 'Ending quantity threshold for a tiered pricing block; null indicates no upper limit.']
  tier_start_quantity decimal(12,4) [note: 'Starting quantity threshold for a tiered pricing block.']
  tou_period_name varchar [note: 'Label for the TOU interval such as "On‑Peak", "Mid‑Peak", or "Off‑Peak".']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Measurement unit used for the component (e.g., kilowatt‑hour for energy, megawatt for demand).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date‑time of the most recent modification to the rate component record.']

  Note: 'Individual pricing component within a rate schedule, defining the specific charge calculation rules for energy (kWh), demand (kW), gas (MCF/Therm), fixed customer charges, taxes, and riders. Captures component type, unit of measure, block tier thresholds, seasonal applicability, rate amount, calculation algorithm reference, and TOU period classification (period name, season, day type, start/end times for on-peak, mid-peak, off-peak, super-peak, critical peak). Enables granular bill calculation, TOU/CPP/RTP interval billing, and rate case modeling.'
}

  last_credit_review_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent comprehensive credit review and risk assessment performed for this counterparty.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this counterparty record, used for change tracking and audit purposes.']
  legal_entity_name varchar [note: 'Full legal name of the counterparty as registered with regulatory authorities and used in master trading agreements.']
  master_agreement_effective_date date [note: 'Date on which the master trading agreement with this counterparty became legally effective and binding.']
  master_agreement_reference_number varchar [note: 'Unique reference number or identifier assigned to the master trading agreement for contract management and trade confirmation purposes.']
  master_agreement_type varchar [note: 'Type of master trading agreement governing transactions with this counterparty: ISDA (International Swaps and Derivatives Association for financial derivatives), NAESB (North American Energy Standards Board for physical gas), EEI (Edison Electric Institute for physical power), WSPP (Western Systems Power Pool), or custom bilateral agreement.']
  moodys_credit_rating varchar [note: 'Current long-term issuer credit rating assigned by Moody\'s Investors Service (e.g., Aaa, Baa2, etc.) used for counterparty credit risk assessment.']
  nerc_registration_code varchar [note: 'NERC-assigned identifier for registered entities subject to Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) standards and reliability compliance.']
  netting_agreement_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator of whether a payment netting agreement is in place allowing offsetting of amounts owed between parties (True = netting agreement exists, False = gross settlement required).']
  next_credit_review_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next periodic credit review and risk reassessment of this counterparty.']
  onboarding_date date [note: 'Date when the counterparty was initially onboarded and approved for trading activity, marking the start of the business relationship.']
  parent_guarantor_name varchar [note: 'Legal name of the parent company or third-party entity providing a guarantee for this counterparty\'s trading obligations, if applicable.']
  primary_contact_email varchar [note: 'Email address of the primary business contact for trade confirmations, scheduling notifications, and operational communications.']
  primary_contact_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the primary business contact for trading operations and contract administration at the counterparty organization.']
  primary_contact_phone varchar [note: 'Business telephone number of the primary contact for urgent trading and operational matters.']
  sp_credit_rating varchar [note: 'Current long-term issuer credit rating assigned by Standard & Poor\'s (e.g., AAA, AA+, BBB-, etc.) used for counterparty credit risk assessment.']
